Fix options: (a) runner rotates its run window on a timer (close+reopen every ~24h) so closed archivable runs are always produced; metrics aggregate by strategy_version across windows. (b) archive+prune frames by AGE from the open run too (partial-run archives; manifest becomes multi-chunk per run). (a) is simpler and keeps the whole-run archive model. Do before any extended unattended period.

title: MariaDB sustains live play; a 'stall' was a REPEATABLE-READ monitoring artifact
detail: Live writes are ~25 ms/frame (frame blob 4.4 ms + 150-400 tile upserts ~15 ms + plain-INSERT executemany), under the ~62 ms frame budget — so NO async queue / Valkey / writer-thread is needed; synchronous writes keep up. The apparent 'stall after ~1000 frames' was NOT real: a reused db.connect() (autocommit=False) held an InnoDB REPEATABLE READ snapshot, so repeated COUNT(*) never advanced. ALWAYS monitor live MariaDB progress with a FRESH connection (or autocommit / READ COMMITTED) per sample.  FIXED IN CODE (0.10.0): connect(readonly=True) on MariaDB was a documented no-op (autocommit=False, InnoDB default REPEATABLE READ), so any reader that outlived its first SELECT froze an MVCC snapshot for the connection's life — the real code-level cause of the 'stall/gated reads'. connect() now opens readonly connections autocommit=True under READ COMMITTED so each SELECT is a fresh snapshot; regression test in tests/test_mariadb_roundtrip.py (live-verified + mutation-checked).
evidence: Killed runs #24/#25 actually reached 3024 / 1865 frames (ticks 411962 / 413060) per fresh-connection queries; benchmark: 200-tile executemany upsert = 15 ms, frame insert = 4.4 ms.

title: Village-frame guild snapshot (chars_here + chars_by_world) undercounts the true live roster
detail: Operator noticed our UI roster (7 = 5 home + 2 fielded) vs the server's own map (28). Investigated run #32: the reported roster (home + fielded, read from the latest village frame's guild snapshot) SWINGS 30->6->30 over ~2400 ticks, but only 5 death events occurred during the 30->6 drop and just 13 recruits all run — so the guild snapshot is NOT tracking real churn; it is a lagged/partial view that momentarily drops live chars (in-transit during rapid embark waves, and worlds its chars_by_world doesn't currently list even though a char is on them). Our per-frame data is internally consistent (village chars_by_world matches the current field frames), so the undercount is in the SERVER's village guild-snapshot cadence, not our parsing. The reliable roster count is DISTINCT live char_uids across a recent window of ALL world frames (=30), not any single village frame. STRATEGY RISK: village() computes roster=len(here)+fielded and fielded from this same snapshot to gate recruit (roster<cap) and embark (fielded+inflight<world_cap) — so an undercount can over-recruit / over-deploy. The UI (metrics.snapshot -> _latest_frame('village')) faithfully shows the dips because it reconnects per refresh (NOT pinned; today's readonly-snapshot fix is unrelated to this). DEEPER ROOT CAUSE (investigated further): the server presents chars INTERMITTENTLY — a live char is absent from ALL received frames for up to ~350 ticks (median max sighting gap 342t among long-lived chars in run #32), and the guild's true roster is LARGE and PERSISTENT across runs (uids up to c7615, far more than the ~13 recruit events this run). So the frame's guild snapshot is an inherently PARTIAL view of a big persistent roster; the 'server map shows 28, our UI shows 7' gap is that the server's map knows the full roster while frames only carry the currently-loaded subset. CONSEQUENCE: the true roster CANNOT be reliably reconstructed from frames — a RosterTracker over any window fails (30t: no change to the dip; 800t: stdev only 6.6->5.6, and dead chars then linger 800t). So a strategy 'fix' to gate recruit/embark on a reconstructed count is NOT achievable and was NOT shipped; 0.10.0's recruit cooldown already curbs the over-recruit (roster_cap 87->11 in run #32). The achievable wins are OBSERVABILITY: an honest UI roster panel (snapshot + recent range + frame age) and a low-noise anomaly on action-error spikes / roster_cap rejections — NOT a reconstructed-count fix.
evidence: run #32: roster trajectory from village frames (30,26,22,20,15,13,8,6,9,25,30) vs 5 deaths + 13 recruits; distinct own uids over last ~50 ticks = 30 while a low village frame reported 6.

title: BUG (fixed): snapshot MIN/MAX(received_at) full-scanned frames (~38s of a ~50s live snapshot)
detail: While adding the roster panel I found metrics.snapshot() takes ~50s on the live MariaDB. Instrumented it: SELECT MIN(received_at) and MAX(received_at) FROM frames were ~19s EACH — received_at is an unindexed double, so each full-scans the large frames table. (My roster/inventory + anomalies_recent additions are ~0.1s, not the cause.) received_at is written monotonically with the autoincrement seq PK, so first/last-by-seq give the same wall span via an index-only PK lookup. Fixed: SELECT received_at FROM frames ORDER BY seq ASC/DESC LIMIT 1. Snapshot 49.7s -> 11.9s, identical result. Same class as finding [19]'s dependent-subquery fix in _run_gold_delta; received_at was the one MIN/MAX left unindexed. Residual ~12s is COUNT(*)/GROUP-BY over the big tables + _run_summaries (~8s over ~30 runs) — acceptable for a background-published snapshot, left for later.
evidence: inline per-statement timing of snapshot() on live MariaDB: min_received 18.9s, max_received 18.7s; after the seq-order rewrite the full snapshot dropped 49.7s->11.9s with wall_seconds unchanged.

title: Poverty trap root cause: a NAV FREEZE — a char re-issues a bounced move forever without learning
detail: The guild collapsed into a poverty trap (0 loot/xp for 8 runs, bare-handed chars, gold 13, village economy at 0). Traced it: a char issues a move into a blocked tile, it bounces (move_failed), and the bot never learns, so it re-issues the SAME doomed move every tick forever. Observed: char c8232 at (43,3) for 40+ ticks, healthy (sta 56), 'pushing north into unexplored ground', never moving. So chars freeze against walls -> never reach loot -> no income -> bare-handed -> spiral. Fixed in GuildBot._field (0.12.0): detect issued-move-but-pos-unchanged, add the tile to a per-world learned-blocked set (TTL 150t) nav routes around.

Also: measure the CURRENT rate of the thing you're fixing before building the fix (cf. the 0.11.x roster_cap miss).

Deploy make bot-restart. Watch: does gold rise once >=15? If it stays ~14 the binding constraint is income, not spending.

title: Iteration 4 candidate: the INCOME half — why do chars barely reach loot (pickup~1)?
detail: Even post-freeze (0.12.0) and with cheap arming (0.13.0), gold may stay pinned if chars don't LOOT. Diagnose pickup~1 over 30k frames: do chars reach loot tiles and fail to pick up, chase receding/contested loot (3-guild world), or die bare-handed before arriving? Then fix (better loot pathing, or don't embark unarmed into a fight). Also ship the sell re-send guard (kills sell_waste=127 / no_such_item). Possibly liquidate the 10 pooled guild potions for bootstrap gold IF guild-inventory selling is feasible (sell is char-scoped — unknown).

title: THE income bottleneck: chars reach loot but bare `pickup` is accepted-with-no-effect (no error, no pickup, carry unchanged)
detail: Traced the pickup failure (run #37): the field is loot-RICH (271 items visible/300 frames), chars DO reach loot tiles (74 char-frames standing ON loot, on plain floor, carry empty 0/24), and issue the canonical bare {action:pickup} (docs 03-actions: 'No item_id: take everything on the tile'; all 3 reference bots do the same). But it produces NO action_error, NO pickup event, and NO carry change — one char sat on ore_copper at (28,10) for 13 consecutive ticks re-issuing pickup, carry stuck 0/24. Only 1 pickup succeeded in 30k frames (a sungrass). Ruled out: reach/movement (they get there), stamina (48>cost), carry-full (empty), wrong tile (floor), wrong action (pickup is right), item_id (docs say bare takes everything). THIS is why the economy can't bootstrap: no loot -> no gold -> no weapons. Item shape has no owner/claim field.
evidence: run #37: 74 on-loot char-frames vs 1 pickup event; c8371 pickup x13 at (28,10) on floor, carry 0/24, 0 pickup errors; item {eid:96937,kind:ore_copper,pos:[28,10]}.

title: WHY is an accepted `pickup` on loot a no-op now? (worked at scale in the single-guild golden era)
detail: An action accepted (no error) but with no effect is unusual. Candidates, needs a LIVE experiment to distinguish: (a) MULTIPLAYER loot contention/ownership — ore dropped by a rival breaking a vein, or contested loot in the now-3-guild world, may be un-pickable by us with no visible marker (golden era with 2110 pickups was single-guild — no rival guild-faction entities in run #22 field frames); (b) a staleness/timing quirk from the MariaDB frame-write latency; (c) a server bug. Graduate to a conjecture with a test, or a discovery once a live probe resolves it. NOTE: could also be that field-loot pickup requires the item's eid explicitly despite the docs (the 1 success grabbed items:[93165] by id) — cheap to test by sending pickup {item_id: eid-underfoot}.
resolution: Refuted: run #52 measured 672 pickups (10.8/1k) — bare pickup works; the low count was crash-loop contamination, not a no-op. See 'measurement artifact' discovery.

title: 0.13.0 partially broke the deadlock: gold 14->34, buys 0->250, pickup 1->8, xp 1->12 (run #38)
detail: The cheap-weapon fix worked partially: the guild scraped enough gold to ARM chars (buy actions jumped from 0 to 250), gold rose from 14 to a max of 34 (first income in 8+ runs), and armed chars started producing a little — pickup 1->8, xp 1->12. Not full recovery (gold ended 7, spent on arming; still poor) but the falsification (gold pinned at 14) did NOT happen. The next drags: a buy/sell re-send storm (fixed in 0.14.0) and the low pickup rate (open).
evidence: run #38 field_productivity: pickup 8, xp 12, buy actions 250, sell 148; gold 14->34->7.

title: Shipped 0.14.0: per-char village-action re-send guard (kills the buy/sell storm)
detail: After a char issues a village action, skip it for VILLAGE_ACTION_COOLDOWN=6 ticks so a stale frame doesn't make it re-issue the same buy/sell/equip. Generalises the embark/recruit in-flight guards to the economy loop. Mutation-checked. Deploy make bot-restart. Watch buy/sell action counts vs real purchases + no_such_item errors.

title: Server now zlib-compresses ZeroMQ wire messages (frames) — decode must decompress (0x78 header)
detail: Mid-session on 2026-08-18 the server started zlib-compressing wire messages. run #38 played uncompressed; the next restart crash-looped on every frame (UnicodeDecodeError byte 0x9c = zlib 0x78 0x9c header) because protocol.decode did a bare json.loads. Fixed (git 7b4dbfe): decode transparently zlib.decompress()es messages starting with 0x78, else plain JSON. encode() unchanged (our uploads stay accepted uncompressed). The server/API/guild were up throughout (a 4th guild g_fd49e0 appeared). Watch for the server also requiring COMPRESSED uploads or a version bump later.
evidence: steemer-live.log crash trace: json.loads UnicodeDecodeError 'byte 0x9c position 1'; zlib.compress header confirmed 0x78 0x9c; run #52 plays after the decode fix.

title: A FOURTH guild appeared (g_fd49e0, ~30 chars) — the world now has 4 guilds
detail: Spectate during the incident: g_cd0e2a (us, 16), g_63837f (30), g_9578ce (1), g_fd49e0 (30). So 4 guilds now (was 3). Consistent with the earlier discovery that guilds are human-spawned and the field keeps filling — more competition for shared loot/space as more humans (often agent-driven) join.
evidence: GET /api/spectate/guilds during the incident listed 4 guild_ids.

title: The 'pickup no-op' was a measurement artifact, not a game bug — looting works fine
body: The premise driving iterations toward an explicit-item_id pickup experiment was false. Run #52 (0.14.0) recorded 672 pickups (10.8/1k frames); every long historical run (run #3 16.98/1k, run #4 ~9.8/1k) also looted healthily. The earlier '~8 pickups/18k frames' reading was contaminated by the empty crash-loop runs #39-#51 (the zlib-incident restarts that stored almost no frames). Bare {action:pickup} is accepted and DOES pick up loot. Lesson: always exclude crash-loop/empty runs before rate-normalising, and re-measure a 'bottleneck' on a clean run before designing an experiment against it.
evidence: metrics.snapshot field_productivity run#52: pickups=672, pickups_per_1k=10.77; events run#52: pickup=687. runs #39-#51 empty (zlib crash-loop).

title: carry.used is WEIGHT, not slot count
body: A live vale char carried 16 inventory items at carry {used:20, cap:21}; another was 23/24 on 12 ore/lumber items. So `used` is a weight sum (items weigh >1) and `cap` varies per char. Consequence: a near-full char that grabs one heavy meat/ore can jump used>cap in a single pickup — you cannot predict fullness from item count.
evidence: run#52 frame decode: eid105243 inv len16 carry 20/21; eid105823 inv len12 carry 23/24.

title: The real income leak: overburden -> strand -> die (loot dies with the char)
body: Run #52 had 1681 `overburdened` events across just 19 chars — one char emitted 939 (stuck ~939 ticks). Overburdened chars can't afford the stamina-gated walk home (server overburden movement penalty) and nothing sheds weight, so they sit burning a scarce world slot (cap 10) until poison (2929 status_damage) finishes them. Only 74 of 687 pickups ever `returned` to be sold (79 sales) — that is why gold stays pinned at ~14 despite healthy looting. Shipped explorer/0.15.0: gate pickup on not-full + drop-to-shed escape when used>=cap.
evidence: run#52 events: overburdened=1681 (top char 939), status_damage=2858/2929dmg, returned=74, sale=79, pickup=687; our char deaths=95 (not 371).

title: `death` events include mobs we KILL (char_uid null) — our true death count is ~4x lower
body: A death event with char_uid null / guild_id null is a monster we killed, not one of our chars dying. Run #52: 371 death events = 95 OUR chars + 288 mob kills (bat_brown 67, skunk 32, wolf 30, ...). Any death-rate metric must filter guild_id==ours / char_uid not null, or it 4x-overstates our losses and understates our combat effectiveness.
evidence: run#52 death events split: ours(char_uid or guild g_cd0e2a)=95, mobs=288.

title: Shipped explorer/0.15.0: full-pickup gate + overburden drop-to-shed escape
body: Two field-strategy changes: (1) pursue/grab loot only when not full (used<cap-1) so chars stop crossing into overburden from a near-full state; (2) when used>=cap, offer `drop` of the least-useful carried item (clutter->ore, never KEEP/gear) above the full-retreat so a stranded char sheds weight and walks its remaining loot home. Deployed to run #54; `drop` actions observed firing in production within minutes. Expect overburden events + our deaths down, returned/sale up toward pickup count, gold accumulating.
evidence: run#54 explorer/0.15.0 live; drop events observed in run#53/#54.

title: svc.sh bot-restart collides with the screen-hosted host (guild single-session kick)
body: The guild server permits ONE live session per guild; a second hello kicks the first ('kicked: another session hello'd as this guild — exiting'). Restarting the bot via svc.sh/`make bot-restart` while the operator's screen 1672.bot host (or its supervisor) is also connected causes a kick war — run #53 played 1865 frames then was kicked; 10 kick lines accumulated before run #54 settled. The detached daemon also doesn't survive the harness cleanly (empty run/bot.pid). Need a single authoritative host: either self-deploy ONLY when the screen host is down, or hand redeploys to the operator's screen. Currently 0.15.0 is live and stable on run #54, but this is fragile.
evidence: steemer-live.log: 'kicked: another session hello'd'; grep -c kicked=10; run#53 kicked mid-run.

title: What exactly is the server's overburden penalty, and what sets per-char carry cap?
body: We infer overburden cripples movement/stamina (stranded chars can't afford the walk home) but haven't measured the penalty curve — is it a flat move-cost multiplier, a stamina-regen cut, or a hard stop? And carry.cap varies per char (21 vs 24 observed) — is it a stat (STR/END?) or gear-driven? Answering both would let us set the not-full threshold precisely and decide whether raising a carry stat/buying a bag beats dropping loot.

title: 0.15.0 measured: cut stuck-overburden but introduced a pickup<->drop thrash (net sales DOWN)
body: Run #55 (0.15.0, 137k frames) vs run #52 (0.14.0, 77k): permanent-stuck overburden fell (overburdened 30->11/1k, status_damage 41->17/1k, ob_max per-char 939->621) and pickups leapt (9.95->59.9/1k) — the drop-to-shed did restore mobility. BUT sale fell 1.14->0.86/1k, returned 1.05->0.92/1k, sale_gold flat (311->301 over 1.76x frames = per-frame income ~halved), gold still ~14, and drop nearly equalled pickup (8190 vs 7029). A partial win with a real income regression. LESSON: measure the FULL effect of a fix, not just its target metric — 0.15.0 improved the number it aimed at while a side-effect quietly hurt the goal (gold).
evidence: run#52 vs #55 field_productivity + event counts (per-1k normalised); drop:pickup ~= 7029:8190 in #55, 0 in #52.

title: pickup<->drop thrash: a shed item lands on the char's own tile and is re-grabbed
body: Event-stream drill on run #55's worst char (eid 109684) showed the loop on a single tile [41,8]: pickup -> overburdened -> drop(itemX) -> pickup (grabs itemX back off own tile) -> overburdened -> drop -> ... item 112203 was dropped/re-grabbed 4+ times in ~20 ticks; the char even thrashed at the village edge [47,0]. Root cause: dropping one item takes carry.used back below cap-1 so the char reads 'not full' and the not-full pickup gate re-opens on the very tile holding the dropped item. Fix (0.16.0): a homing latch that suppresses ALL looting until the char is light again, so a shed item is never re-grabbed.
evidence: run#55 event stream eid109684: drop@[41,8] then pickup@[41,8] alternating; village-edge [47,0] same pattern.

title: Shipped explorer/0.16.0: homing latch to end the pickup<->drop thrash
body: A char that fills up (used>=cap-1) latches into self._homing and stays there — pickup, loot-seeking, container-open, mob-chase, frontier and scout all suppressed — until it is light again (used<=cap*0.5, i.e. after the village sells its haul; hysteresis prevents flicker). While homing it heals/flees if hurt, sheds if overburdened (to stay mobile), defends against adjacent mobs, and otherwise only retreats to the village. Deployed to run #56. Watch next window: drop should collapse toward rare genuine sheds, pickups convert to returned/sale, gold rise.
evidence: run#56 explorer/0.16.0 live; early pickup:drop 3:2 (not 1:1).

title: 0.16.0 homing latch is a DECISIVE win — loot->gold pipeline fixed
body: Run #56 (0.16.0, 60k frames) vs #55 (0.15.0) / #52 (0.14.0), per-1k-frame: drop/pickup 0.86->0.065 (thrash dead); returned 0.91->9.54/1k so ~93% of pickups now reach the village vs ~10% before (returned≈pickup); sale 0.83->3.35/1k; gold income 2.13->10.96/1k (2.7x the 0.14.0 baseline of 4.01); overburdened 10.36->0.38/1k (~eliminated); our deaths 1.40->0.84/1k (-40%); error rate 1.3%. Note the 0.15.0 pickup 60/1k was INFLATED by thrash re-grabs — true pickup rate is ~10/1k and now nearly all of it converts. The overburden->strand->die arc that ran 0.12->0.16 is mechanically CLOSED.
evidence: metrics field_productivity + event counts runs #52/#55/#56, per-1k normalised.

title: Gold balance stays 0-18 because the guild is too poor to buy survival potions
body: Despite 2.7x income, gold oscillates 0..18 (never accumulates): the guild earns ~11/1k and spends it all. It's below the 20g potion price, so fielded chars go out potion-less (1 of 9 carried one) and die to poison (status_damage is the top damage source), dropping gear+loot — a death->reloss treadmill. The spend order arms any bare char (club 15g) before an armed char can reach the potion step (was 25g), and we already hold ~12 armed chars > world_cap (10) — so scarce gold is drained arming bench-warmers we cannot field. Shop prices: club 15, potion_red 20, shortsword 45 (req str4). Fixed in 0.17.0 (survival reserve).
evidence: run#56: gold range 0..18 over 15k village frames; fielded 9 armed 7 potion 1; 112 buys; village armed 5/bare 13; shop buy_price club15/potion20.

title: Shipped explorer/0.17.0: survival reserve + potion at cost
body: POTION_MIN_GOLD 25->20 (buy at the potion's actual price). WEAPON_BUY_RESERVE=20: once the guild has earners (any char fielded or armed), only arm a bare char from gold above the reserve, so the treasury can climb past the potion threshold and armed earners get healed instead of gold draining into bench-warmer clubs. No reserve during the broke-and-bare bootstrap (preserves the 0.13.0 escape). Deployed to run #57. Watch next window: weapon over-buying tapers, potion buys appear, fielded potion-carry rises, deaths fall, gold accumulates off ~14.
evidence: run#57 explorer/0.17.0 live.

title: Where does the recruit churn go? 216 recruits/run vs ~51 deaths, roster_cap ~30
body: Run #56 fired 216 recruit events but only ~51 of our chars died and roster_cap is ~30. If recruiting is free but arming costs 15g each, that's a lot of bare mouths to arm. Need to reconcile: how many recruits actually become living roster members vs fail/expire, does recruit itself cost gold, and is the recruit rate (gated on roster_cap) over-firing? If we're over-recruiting bare chars that never get fielded (world_cap 10), that compounds the gold drain the 0.17.0 reserve targets — a recruit throttle might be the next lever.

title: 0.17.0 survival reserve REGRESSED engagement — reverted in 0.18.0
body: Run #73 (0.17.0, 67k frames) vs run #56 (0.16.0): the WEAPON_BUY_RESERVE drove our deaths to ~0 (0.68->0.01/1k) and collapsed recruit churn (216->21) — but WITH collapsed engagement, not thriving chars: gold income 9.9->2.3/1k, sales 220->46, pickups 9.3->3.1/1k, attacks 79->34/1k; gold still stuck (mean ~9, max 18). Since gold never crosses ~18, the reserve (arm only from gold above one potion) meant a club (15+20 reserve=35) was never affordable, so chars sat idle. Near-zero deaths were an artifact of near-zero activity. Reverted (0.18.0): arm whenever affordable, as in 0.16.0. LESSON (again): measure the FULL effect — a survival metric can improve because chars stopped doing anything.
evidence: run#73 vs #56 field_productivity + econ (per-1k): income 9.94->2.34, sale 220->46, pickup 9.27->3.06, attack 78.6->34.4, deaths 51->1, recruit 216->21.

title: The recruit churn WAS death-replacement (answers the open question)
body: Prior open question: why 216 recruits/run vs 51 deaths? Answer confirmed by 0.17.0: when deaths fell 51->1, recruits fell 216->21 in lockstep. So recruiting is dominated by replacing dead chars, not over-recruiting bare bench-warmers. A stable, surviving roster self-limits recruiting. So a recruit throttle is NOT needed; keeping chars alive is what cuts recruit spend.
evidence: run#56 (0.16.0): 51 deaths / 216 recruits; run#73 (0.17.0): 1 death / 21 recruits.

title: EMBARK<->RETURN churn: full armed chars cycle the field edge without offloading (the real gold blocker)
body: In run #73, 32 surviving chars each embarked ~360x / returned ~130x (11.5k embark events) but only 46 sales — sampled churners were ARMED, full-HP, and FULL of loot (carry 18-23/21-24) in the field, yet not converting to sales. Embarks FAR exceed returns (11.5k vs 3.5k), hinting the embark ACTION is sent redundantly and silently accepted by the server (embark_action_errors=1). NOT a just-returned-not-in-`chars` timing gap: chars_here matched the village `chars` list in 200/200 sampled frames. This churn — full chars failing to reach the village and sell — is the likely reason gold never accumulates across ALL versions (~9, max 18). NEXT LEVER: trace a single full/homing char frame-by-frame from field to village to see why it doesn't offload (does the homing latch clear? does it re-embark before selling? is embark being re-sent while fielded?). This, not the buy-side, is probably the gold blocker.

title: ROOT CAUSE of stuck gold (all versions): unsold FOOD clogs packs -> chars pinned full -> re-embarked off the boundary, never selling
body: Traced run #74's top embarker (c9888, 1183 embarks / ~0 sales): it carried 22-23/24 (FULL) the ENTIRE time, all egg/meat/tomato/berries/turnip (uses:['drink']) + bottles. _should_sell excluded every 'drink' item ('keep food'), but the guild never eats food, so packs fill with unsellable food -> char is permanently `full` (homing) -> in the village it has NO sellable action -> village()'s per-char loop finds nothing to do -> the embark section re-embarks it straight off the y=0 boundary back into the field. It walks to the edge, is yanked back, forever — never offloading. THIS is why gold never accumulated in ANY version (~9, max 18); it was masked by death-churn until 0.17.0's survival exposed it. Food IS sellable (meat/egg/berries among top-sold items historically; the shop buys anything). Fixed in 0.19.0: sell food, keep only KEEP + medicinal drinks (potion*/vial*/elixir*/tonic*).
evidence: run#74 frame trace of c9888: world flickers mines<->village at y=0 while carry stays 22-23/24; inventory = 6 egg+9 meat+tomato+berries+turnip+3 bottle+potion_blue, all drink/KEEP; embark events fire each boundary touch; 1183 embarks vs ~0 sales.

title: Shipped explorer/0.19.0: sell food (unclog the pack, break the embark thrash)
body: _should_sell now keeps only KEEP field supplies and medicinal drinks (DRINK_KEEP_PREFIXES = potion/vial/elixir/tonic); raw food (drink loot) is sold. A returning full-of-food char now has a SELL action in village() so it offloads instead of being re-embarked. Deployed to run #75; early signal ~23 sales/1k vs 0.18.0's 2.3/1k (~10x). Measure next window: sales toward the return rate, embark:return ratio toward 1, gold climbing off ~9. If food turns out to HEAL when eaten, a future lever is drinking it in the field (free heal) rather than only selling.
evidence: run#75 early: 12 sales / 520 frames (~23/1k).

title: MILESTONE: gold finally ACCUMULATES — the poverty arc (0.12->0.19) is closed
body: Run #75 (0.19.0) vs #74 (0.18.0): gold_max 19->542, gold_mean 6.3->99.9 (16x) — gold broke past the ~18 ceiling that held in EVERY prior version (trajectory hits 376/383/529). sale/1k 2.1->9.82 (4.7x), gold_income/1k 6.8->27.1 (4x), embark churn 8101->906 (9x fewer, the thrash is gone), pickups 7.3->13.2/1k and attacks 58.6->88.7/1k recovered. Selling food (0.19.0) was the unlock: chars offload in the village instead of being re-embarked off the boundary. The long poverty arc (nav 0.12 -> buy-weapon 0.13 -> anti-storm 0.14 -> overburden-escape 0.15 -> homing-latch 0.16 -> [0.17 reserve regression, reverted 0.18] -> SELL-FOOD 0.19) is CLOSED end-to-end.
evidence: run#74 vs #75 village-frame gold sampling: max 19->542, mean 6.3->99.9; sale/1k 2.1->9.82; embark 8101->906.

title: Rich but under-equipped: 6/10 fielded chars are BARE, 0 armor, spend_xp never fires
body: Now that gold accumulates (mean 100, max 542), the binding constraint has shifted to EQUIPMENT/GROWTH, not poverty. Snapshot of run #75: 6 of 10 fielded chars BARE-handed, 0 with armor, fielded levels only 2-5. spend_xp fired 0 times (banked XP unused for VIT/END durability); brew/smelt/forge all 0. Cause of bare field: the embark section embarks here_avail[0] with NO armed-status filter, so a bare char gets fielded during a gold-dip (gold oscillates below the 15g club price) before the village arms it, then stays bare (returns are rare). Fix candidate (0.20.0): don't embark BARE chars — keep them home to be armed first (bootstrap exception when no armed char exists) — so the now-affordable arming actually reaches the field. Then upgrade clubs->better weapons (armed chars never upgrade — step 3 only fires when hand is empty) and wire spend_xp.

title: Shipped explorer/0.20.0: field only ARMED chars (spend the gold surplus on a capable field)
body: The embark section now fields only ARMED chars; bare chars wait home to be armed first (now that gold accumulates, arming is affordable). Bootstrap exception: field a bare char only if nothing is fielded AND no armed char is home (cold start). Targets the run-#75 gap (6/10 fielded BARE despite gold 500+). Deployed to run #76. Measure next: fielded-armed fraction toward 100%, deaths down, kills/income up. Follow-on levers if this lands: upgrade clubs->better weapons (armed chars never upgrade — buy only fires when hand is empty), wire spend_xp (fired 0x — banked XP unused), and M3a forge for armor (0 armor; blocked on a per-world product name).
evidence: run#76 explorer/0.20.0 live.

title: 0.20.0 armed-only field EMPTIED the field (reverted in 0.21.0)
body: Run #76 (0.20.0) vs #75 (0.19.0): fielding only armed chars dropped fielded_mean 9.9->1.8 — the guild holds only ~4 armed chars, so removing the bare 'padding' collapsed the field to ~2. Income cratered: sale/1k 9.18->2.84, gold_mean 93.7->6.5, gold_max 530->13 — back to poverty, a death spiral (empty field->no income->no gold->can't arm->field stays empty). LESSON: a bare char in the field still picks up loot and holds a slot — better than empty. Fielding is not the place to gate equipment. Reverted to fielding any available char (0.19.0). run #77 confirms the field refills to 10 immediately.
evidence: run#76 vs #75: fielded_mean 9.9->1.8, gold_mean 93.7->6.5, gold_max 530->13, sale/1k 9.18->2.84.

title: Shipped explorer/0.21.0: revert 0.20.0 — field any available char again
body: Restores the 0.19.0 milestone gains (gold accumulation). run #77 field back to 10. The equipment lever must improve chars WITHOUT shrinking the field: (a) upgrade weapons on already-fielded/armed chars (club->shortsword/bow when affordable+qualified — buy step currently only fires when hand is empty), (b) wire spend_xp (fired 0x — banked XP unused for durability), (c) M3a forge for armor (blocked on a per-world product name). Do NOT gate who gets fielded. Also OPEN: why does the guild hold only ~4 armed chars? arming should outpace ~10 field slots given gold surplus — investigate whether chars lose weapons (death drops) or arming is too slow.

title: Partial recovery: run #77 gold stuck (mean 8.6) because deaths doubled (38->80) — poison churn
body: 0.21.0 (== 0.19.0 economics) refilled the field but gold did NOT recover to run #75's level (mean 93.7/max 530) — run #77 mean 8.6/max 48. Cause: OUR deaths doubled 38->80 (status_damage/1k 26.9->50.3; death positions at low-y = dying mid-retreat), spawning 303 recruits that keep the roster young (lvl 2-6) and weak, capping income. The 0.20.0 spiral wiped the veteran roster; the young replacement churns on poison. Only 1/10 fielded carry a potion; potion supply (18 brewed + few bought, gold-limited) << poison demand. It is NOT a transient dip — gold stayed low across the whole 60k-frame run.
evidence: run#77 vs #75: our_deaths 80 vs 38, status_damage/1k 50.3 vs 26.9, gold_mean 8.6 vs 93.7, recruits 303 vs 179.

title: Shipped explorer/0.22.0: spend_xp affordability fix (may be partly inert — verify)
body: _pick_xp_stat now returns the highest-priority stat that is BOTH below cap AND affordable with banked XP (was: top-priority regardless of cost, so a char stuck on an unaffordable VIT never spent its XP — spend_xp = 0 across all history). Correct + mutation-tested. BUT run #78 shows spend_xp still 0 at 4k frames despite chars with xp 113/242 existing — likely because those xp-rich chars are perpetually-FIELDED veterans that rarely visit the village, while village chars are fresh recruits with xp~0 (auto-consumed by leveling/stat_up). So the fix may be largely inert. VERIFY NEXT PASS: does spend_xp go >0 over a full run? If still 0, the real blocker is that chars don't return to the village to invest XP (or re-embark before an idle spend_xp tick after selling) — fix by letting a returning char spend_xp during its sell-visit (e.g. before re-embark, or exempt spend_xp from VILLAGE_ACTION_COOLDOWN). If spend_xp fires, watch deaths fall.

title: Worsening poison-death spiral: deaths/1k 0.57->1.33->1.57, gold stuck ~7, roster ~8
body: Runs #75->#77->#78: our deaths/1k climbed 0.57->1.33->1.57 (NOT recovering). Root: chars poisoned deep (death y median 28) die mid-retreat before reaching the poison-clearing village (village chars = 0% poison; home is safe, they can't reach it). Roster collapsed to ~8 (all fielded; VILLAGE IS EMPTY), so village economy (brew/spend_xp/arm/heal) barely runs. Gold stuck ~7 — all income drained re-arming 268 dying recruits (15g clubs). Survival supplies unaffordable: potion 20g, brew bottle 2g but gated at BREW_MIN_GOLD 10, and chars hold 0 herbs/0 potions. spend_xp confirmed INERT (0 over 65k frames — xp-rich chars are fielded, village chars have xp~0). Self-reinforcing: young roster -> poison deaths -> churn -> no accumulation -> no survival supplies -> more deaths.
evidence: run#78: our_deaths 103 (1.57/1k), gold_mean 7.1/max14, roster ~8 lvl1-5, status poison 1438/burn 262, village 0 chars sampled, spend_xp 0.

title: Shipped explorer/0.23.0: un-healed chars stay shallow (survive the poison-retreat)
body: An un-healed char (no potion_red) past POISON_SAFE_DEPTH (12) stops pushing into frontier/unexplored ground and heads HOME instead — a short survivable retreat vs the median-28-deep deaths. Adjacent loot/attack still outscore it (opportunistic); a char carrying a heal may range deep (drink en route). Gold-free, no field-size effect (0.20.0 lesson), no gold drain (0.17.0 lesson). Deployed to run #79. MEASURE next: deaths/1k down from 1.57? roster growing past ~8? gold climbing off 7? If deaths fall, the churn should unwind and gold accumulate. If not, the poison spiral may need a supply-side fix (lower BREW_MIN_GOLD to 2-4 so the poor guild can brew, but chars also hold 0 herbs — herbs get sold/lost to the churn).

title: Death-spiral root cause: RISING UNDEAD (poison mobs) via band-refresh + a broke guild that can't fund survival; inflection at run #77
body: Traced deaths/1k across all runs. It correlates with UNDEAD-mob prevalence (cultist/zombie/ghoul/vampire_bat/cinder_wisp — the poison/burn dealers spawned by the periodic band_refresh mechanic, ~24-88 refreshes/run). Undead share of field mobs has TRENDED UP: run74 17% -> 75 16% -> 77 22% -> 78 22% -> 79 35%, and deaths/1k track it: 0.32 -> 0.57 -> 1.21 -> 1.83 -> 2.74. THE INFLECTION is run #77 (0.21.0, 08-19 07:20): deaths jumped 0.57->1.21. Crucially run #77 uses the SAME code as run #75, so our code did NOT cause it. Two co-factors: (1) WORLD (external): undead/poison bands rising. (2) GUILD (broke): the run-#75 'milestone' gold was TRANSIENT — gold spiked to ~314-530 in the first ~third then COLLAPSED to ~10 by mid-run and never recovered; gold has sat ~10 across runs 76-79. So the guild can't afford potions(20g)/gear to survive the undead. Pivotal self-inflicted event: run #76 (0.20.0 armed-only-field) wasted 68min with an empty field, squandering the one window where gold had accumulated. Net: rising poison waves hitting a chronically broke/young/potion-less roster -> mass deaths -> recruit churn -> stays broke -> worse each run. 0.23.0's shallow-venture (keep un-healed chars away from deep mobs) is a reasonable response but likely insufficient vs a 35%-undead world.
evidence: per-run deaths/1k vs undead%: (74,0.32,17),(75,0.57,16),(76,0.02,10=empty-field),(77,1.21,22),(78,1.83,22),(79,2.74,35). gold trace run75: @25%=314,@mid=10,@end=9. enemy comp run75=skunk/boar/cow/wildlife vs run79=cultist/ghoul/zombie.

title: Gold-source map: field coins (instant-banked, ~50%) + chests (direct 1-21g + loot); no shop arbitrage; no confirmed gold cap
body: Investigated all gold mechanics. (1) FIELD GOLD COINS: ~half of income (4729g/1436 coins, avg 3.3, max 67); gold is currency not a carried item, so it BANKS TO THE TREASURY INSTANTLY (death-proof); only ~3% of coins coincide with a kill, so grabbable without fighting = the ideal easy/consistent/safe source. (2) CHESTS: the `opened` event carries {loot:[...], gold:1-21} — direct gold PLUS loot (tomes/charms/gems/bombs/ore); ~39 chests/run, renewed each band_refresh, each opens exactly once (no camp-farm). High-value SELLABLES are all chest loot: tomes 24-44g, sun/moon charms 30g, gems ~5g (vs meat/lumber/egg 1-2g). (3) NO NPC ARBITRAGE: shop sell_price is always ~20% of buy_price; smelting ore->ingot is break-even-to-loss. (4) PLAYER MARKET empty (market_listings=[]) — no arbitrage now, untapped. (5) GOLD CAP: none confirmed — most ever held is 529 (run #75); we've never had enough to test. Test it by stockpiling past ~529.
evidence: sale-by-item runs74+ (tome_ring avg 44, sun_charm 30); gold events 1436 coins 4729g, 3% near a death; opened payloads {gold:18/21,loot:[...]}, 39 distinct chest pos each opened once; shop sell~=0.2*buy; guild.market_listings=[]; max gold observed 529 run75.

title: Shipped explorer/0.24.0: GOLD-RUSH — beeline coins/chests, no combat-chase, freeze potion/bottle buys
body: Per operator directive (prioritise grabbing & stockpiling gold vs fighting the undead world). FIELD: beeline to gold coins (5.0) then chests (4.5) over loot (4.0); crack adjacent chest = top priority (7.0); NO monster-chase (removed close-to-enemy; adjacent-attack 8.0 still defends). VILLAGE HOARD: froze potion + bottle buys; kept the 15g club for bare chars (operator's call) + free brewing with held bottles. Deployed to run #80. MEASURE next: gold_mean/max climbing (does it break 529 -> is there a cap?), field-gold + chest-open rates up, deaths (should fall — not chasing undead), and whether the hoard actually accumulates or still leaks (recruit re-arming). Follow-ups: player-market listing of tomes/charms; sell ore raw (smelt is a loss).

title: Band-refresh cycle is periodic (~14.4-15.6k ticks) and ANNOUNCED — analysable for undead-rush prediction
body: The maps repopulate per-BAND: each world has 4 bands (0-3) that refresh independently every ~14400-15600 ticks (regular). The game gives ADVANCE NOTICE: the frame carries `next_refresh {band, in_ticks}` (next refresh per world) and emits `band_refresh_warning {band, world, in_ticks:240}` ~240 ticks before, plus `band_refresh_deferred {in_ticks:120}` (deferred while a char is in the band) and `band_refresh {band, world}` on the event. A refresh rotates the mob set between benign wildlife and poison undead. We can't yet PREDICT the new mood from the event (band+timing only, not the incoming mob type) — that needs learning the band->type pattern over cycles (record it going forward). But LIVE mood is directly observable (mob kinds in view), and refreshes are periodic + pre-warned, so behavior can adapt and even pre-empt (evacuate a band about to refresh). 0.25.0 uses live mood; the loop should keep logging band composition to learn the pattern.
evidence: band_refresh intervals per (world,band) ~14400-15600 ticks; next_refresh={'band':3,'in_ticks':641}; band_refresh_warning in_ticks=240; band_refresh_deferred in_ticks=120.

title: Shipped explorer/0.25.0: mood-driven drastic undead-flee
body: When a THREAT mob (undead: cultist/zombie/ghoul/vampire_bat/cinder_wisp/skeleton/wraith/lich/...) is within FLEE_RADIUS(4), a healthy char FLEES to the village and does NOT loot/fight — snatches only an underfoot coin (instant banked) on the way, fights only if cornered. Homing chars exempt. When no threat near (wildlife band), 0.24.0 gold-rush runs. So behavior adapts to band mood: evade rushes, harvest calm bands. NOTE: 0.24.0 gold-rush measured NO improvement in its first ~10min (run #80) — but run #80 was a 100%-undead band (worst case). Deployed 0.25.0 to run #81. MEASURE next over a FULL band cycle: does gold accumulate during wildlife windows / survive undead windows? deaths/1k down? gold break 529 (cap test)?

title: API security review -> server_bugs.md (3 issues for the dev)

title: 0.25.0 undead-flee halved deaths (2.74->1.02/1k) but gold still stuck (~10) — world undead-heavy most of the time

title: Shipped explorer/0.26.0: safe-world routing + loosened flee (grab safe-direction gold)
body: (1) Track per-world undead fraction (self._world_threat, expires THREAT_TTL=1200); embark routes chars to the SAFEST world (lowest undead), concentrating the guild in the wildlife world / out of undead ones. (2) A fleeing char may still fetch a coin farther from every threat than it is (safe direction), recovering income during undead bands. Deployed to run #82. MEASURE next: does gold finally accumulate (does the guild cluster in the safe world)? break 529? deaths stay low? Watch a failure mode: if ALL worlds are undead, routing can't help (all bad) and the re-scout TTL may cause some churn.

title: 0.26.0 safe-world routing works (deaths 1.02->0.2/1k, chars cluster in wildlife) but gold plateaued — drain is RECRUITING+arming
body: Run #82 (0.26.0): deaths cratered to 0.2/1k (5x better than 0.25.0); clustering confirmed — when spire hit 100% undead, chars fled it and piled into vale+mines (0% undead), spire 1->0 of our chars. Chest-opens 5 (was 1), field-coin 163g. But gold still ~11 (max 51). Net flow: income 362g/run (sales 114 + coins 165 + chests 83) but gold cycles 0->14->buy-a-15g-club->0. Recruiting is FREE (delta 0 at recruit ticks) but fired toward the server's high cap (roster grew to 23 while we field only ~10 = party_cap 5 x 2 safe worlds), and each new bare recruit gets a 15g club -> income cycles straight back out. THE drain.
evidence: run#82: deaths 9/45k=0.2/1k; chars_by_world clustered off the 100%-undead spire; gold IN 362 (114+165+83); recruits 66, roster now 23, field 10; gold trajectory cycles to 0 on club buys.

title: Shipped explorer/0.27.0: cap recruiting at fieldable size (party_cap*maps+bench) to stop the club-arming drain
body: Recruit only up to party_cap*len(maps)+RECRUIT_BENCH(2) instead of the server's roster/world cap, so we stop growing an undeployable bench that each needs a 15g club. Keeps the operator's 'club per char' (existing chars stay armed) — just stops recruiting chars we can't field. Deployed run #83. MEASURE next: does gold FINALLY accumulate off ~11 and break 529 (the cap test) now that income isn't recycled into clubs? does the roster settle ~15-17? deaths stay ~0.2/1k? If gold still stuck, the club-buy itself may need freezing (revisit with operator, who chose to keep clubs).

title: 0.27.0: gold now peaks 155 (up from 51) but the club-buy is the whole remaining drain (390g/run) — an operator decision (freeze clubs?)
body: Run #83 (0.27.0): income up (607g/run — chests now 211g). Every gold DROP is exactly -15 coinciding with a `buy` -> 100% club-buying, 26 clubs = 390g/run, the ONLY spending. Gold reaches 155 mid-run then bleeds back to ~14 on clubs. True roster is only ~12 (10 fielded vale+mines + 2 home; the '30' was count-flicker) but we RECRUITED 42x while only 14 died -> ~28 recruits vanish (roster-churn: recruit->arm->vanish->recruit), each getting a 15g club. And chars barely FIGHT now (attacks 21/1k, down from 66) — they flee undead and loot wildlife, so the clubs are nearly dead weight. So the stockpile is blocked ONLY by club-buying. The operator explicitly chose 'keep a club per char' (over total-hoard and hoard-above-reserve); freezing club-buying would make net income ~+607g/run and stockpile fast (break 529). Surfaced to the operator as their decision — NOT shipped unilaterally. Deaths stayed low (0.3/1k); safe-world routing still working.

title: 0.28.0 shipped: froze the weapon-buy (FREEZE_WEAPON_BUY) — pure hoard, the sole 390g/run drain is gone
body: Acting on the run#83 discovery that the club-buy was the only treasury drain (26 clubs=390g/run, gold peaked 155 then bled to ~2). FREEZE_WEAPON_BUY=True gates off the last village spend line (potion/bottle already frozen 0.24.0). Justified because clubs are near-dead weight post-flee (attacks 21/1k, ~28/42 recruits churn out before fighting) and only ~3% of gold is kill-tied. Deployed run #84. FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION: run#84+ gold climbs monotonically (no -15 drops) and breaks 529 (cap test — a fixed plateau = the gold cap). Falsified if gold still bleeds (missed spend path) or income craters (no kill-drops at all). Named tradeoff: a 0-armed-char collapse can't auto-arm (0.13.0 bootstrap) — flip the flag to restore. Operator decided autonomously under the new 10-min no-hang rule (their 'extraordinarily drastic hoard' directive over the older 'keep 1 club/char').

title: 0.28.0 freeze CONFIRMED the stockpile (gold median 2->92, zero drops) but a poison cycle spiked deaths 10x — poison DoT, not combat [CORRECTED iter20: death cause was NOT poison DoT but UNRECOGNISED MELEE PREDATORS (golem_stone/delver/boar) in the 0%-undead wildlife worlds; the undead-fraction link was spurious. See 0.30.0 + the real-cause discovery.]
body: Run #84 (0.28.0 pure hoard): gold mean 5.7->68.3, median 2->92, last 173, climbing past the old 155 peak with 0 gold drops (26 clubs/run drain eliminated). Payoff CONFIRMED. BUT deaths jumped 0.2->2.23/1k in a poison-heavy band cycle (field undead 1.6% in calm run #82 -> 9.3% in #84). Deaths are POISON DoT, not combat: 21/22 sampled had no undead adjacent; two traces show steady hp bleed (18->12->6->3; 6->2->1) with status=None, potion-less packs (potion-buy frozen since 0.24.0), one dying 1 tile short of the vale edge, one STUCK deep at [54,11] not moving while bleeding. Roster stayed healthy (28: 18 home+10 fielded) and banked gold is death-proof (dying chars carry nothing, dropped:[]), but income HALVED (607->269g, chest-opens 10->3) because dead/fleeing chars stop looting — throttling the stockpile. Fix shipped 0.29.0: heal from surplus (potion-buy gated on POTION_RESERVE 100).

title: 0.29.0 shipped: heal-from-surplus (POTION_RESERVE=100) to counter the poison deaths without breaking the hoard [CORRECTED iter20: death cause was NOT poison DoT but UNRECOGNISED MELEE PREDATORS (golem_stone/delver/boar) in the 0%-undead wildlife worlds; the undead-fraction link was spurious. See 0.30.0 + the real-cause discovery.]
body: Un-froze the potion-buy behind a reserve floor: buy a potion-less char a heal only while gold-price>=100, so the stockpile floor holds and climbs while earners stay alive. Bounded (<=1 potion/char, gated) unlike the old club drain. Deployed run #85. Prediction: deaths -> ~0.2-0.3/1k, income recovers, gold still climbs above 100 toward 529. Uncertainty (medium): a heal only helps FLEEING poisoned chars (buys ticks to reach safety); it does NOT help a char stuck deep bleeding without moving (saw one at [54,11]) — if deaths stay high, the residual is nav/depth (lower POISON_SAFE_DEPTH or fix the stuck-flee), or go structural with band PRE-EMPTION (evacuate a world before it turns undead using next_refresh/band_refresh_warning).
test: run#85+ deaths/1k vs 2.23; income vs 269; gold trajectory vs the 100 floor; potion buys appear; do stuck-deep bleed-outs persist?

title: REAL death cause = unrecognised MELEE predators in the 0%-undead wildlife worlds (golem_stone/delver/boar), NOT poison [UPDATE iter21: block-adjacent VALIDATED — golem HP-drops 28->0, no boxing-in (move_failed fell). Residual: delver/boar drift onto stationary chars (mob-approach, not ours) + new killers spider/wolf/crab -> 0.31.0 adds a dodge-when-adjacent + those kinds.]
body: Run #85: safe-world routing works (chars cluster vale/mines at 0% undead, shun spire 100%), yet deaths stayed 2.23/1k and 12/13 were in MINES (0% undead). Killer traced: a full-HP char (24/24) steps adjacent to a golem_stone and takes -15 in one tick, then dies. Burst MELEE not poison DoT (0.29 heal useless — can't outrun a 2-hit kill). Empirical blame of every big HP-drop (>=5/tick) on the nearest non-wildlife mob within dist 2: delver 36, golem_stone 28, boar 18, lake_drake 5, drake 3 (~84%) + spire undead 9. The 0.25 undead=threat/wildlife=safe model was INCOMPLETE. Fix 0.30.0: MELEE_THREAT_KINDS + block-adjacent pathing (route around, not radius-flee, to keep looting).
evidence: run#85: deaths 12/13 in mines(0% undead); golem trace hp 24->9(-15) on stepping adjacent; HP-drop(>=5) adjacency blame delver36/golem28/boar18/lake_drake5/drake3; per-world undead vale0/mines0/spire100%.

title: Diagnostic method: blame big HP-drops (>=5/tick) on the nearest non-wildlife mob within dist 2 to find the true killer
body: The method that caught the melee predators after undead-fraction misled us: walk field frames, detect per-char HP drops >=5 in one tick, attribute to the closest non-benign entity within Manhattan dist 2 in the prior frame. Counts reveal true killers empirically, independent of any hardcoded threat list. Re-run after a band shift to catch a new predator before adding it to MELEE_THREAT_KINDS/THREAT_KINDS.
evidence: applied run#85 -> delver36/golem28/boar18/lake_drake5/drake3 vs a THREAT set that listed none of them; matched the golem_stone death trace.

title: 0.31.0 shipped: dodge-when-a-melee-predator-is-adjacent + add spider/wolf/crab to the avoid set [RESOLVED iter22: dodge/block mechanism WORKS (delver 25->0, spider 6->0) but the DENYLIST was doomed — run#87 brought new lava_ant/rhino_beetle. Inverted to a benign allowlist in 0.32.0. Residual: single-step dodge trades 1:1 vs same-speed chasers (63% still-adjacent).]
body: 0.30.0's block-adjacent solved STATIONARY predators (golem 28->0 drops) but not mobs that DRIFT onto a stationary/looting char (delver 25, boar 13 still hit in run #86). 0.31.0: on adjacency, step to the tile farthest from all predators and never attack them; add spider_brown/wolf/crab_green (run#86 blame). Deployed run #87. NOTE the confounder: run#86 was 45% undead (vs 12.2%) so deaths (2.85/1k) must be read relative to the world's poison level. Uncertainty medium: if these mobs move at char speed the dodge only trades 1:1 — then widen to a step-2 berth or a small radius-flee for the fastest ones. Re-run the HP-drop-blame diagnostic on #87.
test: run#87+ HP-drop blame for delver/boar/spider/wolf vs run#86 (25/13/6/3); deaths/1k normalised by undead %; income/chest-opens not cratered; gold still >=100 floor climbing.

title: Spectate exposes NO mob/tile data and lags 45s — useless for tactical threat-sight; char sight has range ~8-12 tiles but is partly occluded (~18% of mobs first-seen at dist 0)
body: Answering: can spectate give bots better threat-sight? NO. /api/spectate/guilds returns only ROSTERS: per-char {world, level, look, equipment} + per-guild world counts + maps sizes + tick. NO char positions (x,y), NO hp, and NO mobs/entities/tiles. /api/tiles is just the sprite VOCABULARY; our own tiles_seen is accumulated from OUR frames. So the ONLY source of mob positions is a char's own field frames (LOS-limited). TIME DELAY is decisive: SpectateRoster polls every 45s (DEFAULT_POLL_SECONDS=45, stale at 3x=135s) while ZMQ frames are real-time (sub-second) — a 45s-old snapshot is tactically worthless even if it had mobs. Spectate's right use is SLOW strategic signals (roster size, rival world-spread), which we already do. On char sight: frames are per-tick DELTAS accumulating into a known-map; mobs are first-seen at a median 8 tiles (p90 12, max 16) so chars usually see threats coming — BUT ~18% (12/68) first appear at distance 0, consistent with line-of-sight OCCLUSION (a predator hidden behind a wall/corner until rounded) and/or in-place spawns. The 0.31.0 dodge-on-adjacency is the correct mitigation for those sudden-adjacency mobs. Actionable idea (unshipped): a short-TTL MEMORY of recently-seen predator tiles so a char keeps avoiding a spot a golem just vanished behind a wall from (like STUCK_BLOCK), caveated because mobs move.
evidence: spectate roster char record has keys {char_uid,name,level,world,look,equipment} only, no x/y/hp/mobs; DEFAULT_POLL_SECONDS=45; mob first-seen dist median 8/p90 12/max 16 with 12/68 at dist 0; frames delta:True accumulate known-map.

title: Denylist threat model is structurally doomed — every band rotates in NEW predators; inverted to a benign allowlist (default-dangerous)
body: Run #87: the dodge+block ZEROED the cataloged killers (delver 25->0, spider_brown 6->0, wolf 3->1) — mechanism validated. But deaths ROSE to 4.0/1k (0.144 per undead-pt vs 0.063 in #86) because the band brought NEW predators lava_ant (40 HP-drops) + rhino_beetle (7), in no set. A hardcoded MELEE_THREAT_KINDS is always a cycle behind. 0.32.0 inverts: monster = predator by DEFAULT (block-adjacent+dodge) unless in WILDLIFE_SAFE (turtle/chicken/cow/sheep/frog/skunk/rat_grey/mole/bat_brown) or THREAT_KINDS undead (radius-4 flee). ctx.enemies is faction==monster only, so 'not benign = hostile' is safe. Known residuals: (a) single-step dodge trades ~1:1 vs same-speed chasers (63% still-adjacent next tick; boar rose 13->20); (b) cinder_wisp (undead) caused 39 drops despite the radius-4 flee (fast?).
evidence: run#87 HP-drop blame lava_ant40/cinder_wisp39/boar20/none18/cultist16 vs run#86 delver25/boar13/spider6; delver/spider/wolf fell to ~0; deaths 4.0/1k up from 2.85; 1:1-trade 148/235=63% still-adjacent.

title: 0.32.0 allowlist inversion CLOSED the death arc (deaths 3.2->1.7/1k at constant undead) but trades income for survival (income -53%, chests -69%)
body: Run #88 measured (allowlist: monster=predator-by-default). Deaths 3.2->1.7/1k while the undead chars ACTUALLY FACE held ~constant (5.3->5.6% frame-proportional — note this differs from the per-world-equal 75%, which over-weights the abandoned 100%-undead spire; frame-proportional is the honest 'what chars encounter'). Whack-a-mole stopped: HP-drops 156->50, lava_ant 40->11, rhino_beetle gone; 1:1-trade 63->42%; move_failed 26->5/1k. So the structural fix works. BUT the new KPI alarm flagged income -53% (458->215) and chest_opens -69% (13->4) at that ~constant undead -> 0.32.0 OVER-AVOIDS: block-adjacent on EVERY non-benign mob routes chars around too much, so they reach fewer chests. gold_mean held (~100 floor) so the stockpile LEVEL is unhurt, but growth is capped. NEXT: lighten the avoidance footprint (block-adjacent for confirmed-dangerous only + dodge-only for unknowns?) to recover income without losing survival.
evidence: run#88 vs #87: deaths 1.7 vs 3.2/1k; HP-drops 50 vs 156; income 215 vs 458; chest_opens 4 vs 13; undead_frac(frame-prop) 5.6 vs 5.3%; move_failed 5 vs 26/1k; gold_mean 99.7 vs 98.7.

title: 0.33.0 shipped: chest-access exemption + crack/grab-before-dodge to recover the income 0.32.0's over-avoidance gave up
body: KPI alarm flagged 0.32.0 cut income -53%/chest_opens -69% at constant undead (over-avoidance). 0.33.0: exempt only chest-ACCESS tiles from the predator block (chests worth a hit; coins not), and crack-adjacent-chest + grab-underfoot-coin before dodging. Deployed run #89. Prediction: chest_opens/income recover toward pre-0.32 with deaths holding ~1.7/1k (KPI alarm watching). Uncertainty medium: if chests are often boxed by STRONG mobs, the one-hit-to-crack could raise deaths -> then gate the chest-reach on hp>threshold; if income doesn't recover, the loss was coin-traversal not chests.
test: run#89 KPI alarm: chest_opens vs 4, income vs 215, deaths vs 1.7/1k (must not regress); HP-drop blame stable.

title: BUG (operator-observed): a low-stamina char adjacent to a predator RESTS and takes hits — the 1.5x move-stamina margin starved its escape
body: Operator saw a wolf attack a char that neither fled nor fought. Data: run#88 had 437 wolf-adjacent char-frames, char failed to move 62% (113 low-sta-stuck); stamina-when-adjacent median 36/min 6; raw move cost 20, 1.5x margin=30. A char with 12-29 stamina couldn't afford the margined dodge-MOVE -> rested adjacent to the predator. Same starvation hit the undead-flee and hurt-retreat (all survival MOVES gated by the margin). Fix 0.34.0: offer(urgent=True) for survival moves -> raw cost, no margin. Below the raw move cost (~<12) resting is still forced.

title: REFUTED method: single-frame known-map cannot judge 'cornered' — 83% of death-neighbours are unseen, 0 are known walls
body: Attempted to classify our 51 #92 deaths into cornered / out-of-stamina / had-exit-didnt-move using nav.is_walkable on the neighbours of the death position. v1 reported 42/42 stuck deaths 'cornered' (0 walkable exits). v2 decomposed WHY each neighbour was unwalkable and exposed the confound: across the 42 cornered deaths (168 neighbour-tiles) the make-up was walkable 0, SOLID 0, occupied 28, UNKNOWN 140. Zero known walls + 83% unseen means the single-frame visible.tiles (sparse/incremental by design — the bot accumulates it into `known`) cannot determine walkability. So 'cornered' was a reconstruction artifact, not a real diagnosis. Robust facts that survive: 80% of deaths are STUCK (position-based), ~37% predator-adjacent at death. The valid next diagnostic streams each world's frames accumulating the known-map, then evaluates neighbours against THAT. A 0.37 anti-stuck DESIGN is premature until that runs.

title: Testing gap: seeded 1-frame DB fixtures are BLIND to performance — a data-volume-scaling endpoint (codex, ~17s live) looked instant in tests
body: The Codex decoded a large frame sample synchronously per request; it blocked ~17s on the live DB but every test/smoke used a 1-frame seeded DB where LIMIT-N decodes are instant, so the latency was invisible. Compounded by: I bumped the cost param (sample 1500->4000) AFTER my only live run (which checked output not time) and re-tested only on the seeded DB; and no test measured response time (correctness oracle != performance oracle). Fix: off-thread background build + per-run cache (api_codex returns ~0.13s). Durable lesson: for any endpoint whose cost scales with data volume, TIME it against the LIVE DB before shipping, especially after changing a sample/limit/window; seeded fixtures hide it. Mirror the existing off-thread /api/snapshot pattern for heavy dashboard endpoints from the start.

title: ROOT-CAUSE fix of the stuck-death (0.42.0, run #100): stamina-bounces were poisoning walkable tiles via learned-block (9687 stamina errs vs ~0 wall on #99), walling hurt chars into dead-ends to rest and die; now gated on the move-failure reason + a desperation-escape net
detail: Diagnosed all 8 run#99 our-deaths: NOT combat-seek (every victim hurt<60%, combat-seek gate inactive; died RESTING at full stamina while a wolf pack cornered them). Root: STUCK_BLOCK learned-block blacklisted any tile a move failed to land on, never checking why; ~all #99 move failures were not_enough_stamina (frame-stale margin), so it blacklisted good 'path' tiles for 150 ticks. Recruit-15172 rested at (24,26) sta48 refusing a clear 'path' at (24,25) it had stamina-bounced -> died one step from safety. Fix: on_action_error records per-char reason; skip learn-block on not_enough_stamina (stamina margin already prevents re-issue). Net: DESPERATION ESCAPE steps a hurt+cornered char onto any clear non-wall neighbour (even unseen). Validated on real frames: victim now MOVE:S instead of REST. 4 mutation-checked tests; 296 local/302 reaper.
next: measure #100: our-death/1k toward ~0? move_failed down (fewer wrongly-blocked tiles)? recruiting-churn eases if deaths drop?
