title: All three services found down and the bot then CRASH-LOOPED (exit 139): a FreeBSD update replaced CPython 3.15.0rc1, uv rebuilt .venv and reinstalled a CACHED pyzmq wheel built against the older prerelease, so zmq_getsockopt(ZMQ_TYPE) segfaulted on every start.
detail: Bisected precisely: `import zmq` OK, Context() OK, backend Socket() OK, socket.get(zmq.TYPE) SEGV. Wheel tag cp315-cp315-freebsd_15_1_release_p2_amd64, Generator scikit-build-core (built locally, cached by uv). Fix = rebuild from source against the live interpreter (uv pip install --no-cache --no-binary pyzmq --force-reinstall) AND purge the poisoned cache entry (uv cache clean pyzmq --force -- running services hold a shared cache lock). Recurrence risk: ANY future interpreter change repeats this, which is why the supervisor now runs a smoke test and can repair.
so_what: Prereleased interpreters + locally-compiled wheels + uv's build cache = a silent landmine on every OS update. The smoke test in steemer/health.py is the standing oracle for it.

title: Named the mechanism behind the long-standing 'svc.sh down bot leaves steemer.runner alive' gotcha: daemon(8) records the CHILD pid, but the process GROUP LEADER is daemon itself, so `kill -TERM -$pid` signalled a group that does not exist and the fallback killed only run-live.sh.
detail: Live proof on the running bot: pidfile 2510, pgid 2508. The orphaned uv+python kept playing, which is what produced the redeploy kick-wars and the manual kill-the-remnants dance in HANDOFF. Fixed by resolving the real pgid via `ps -o pgid=` plus a descendant-tree walk, with survivors REPORTED rather than swallowed.
so_what: The documented manual redeploy dance (capture OLD pids, svc.sh down, kill OLD, confirm zero) is no longer needed -- but keep verifying via DB freshness, not the log.

title: svc.sh down failed OPEN where ps(1) is absent: it derived process existence from ps, so 'no ps installed' was indistinguishable from 'process gone' -- it printed 'stale pidfile, pid gone' for a LIVE service, stopped nothing, and exited 0.
detail: Found by the reaper gate, whose debian-slim image ships no procps. Existence now comes from POSIX `kill -0`; where ps is genuinely unavailable svc.sh REFUSES loudly instead of guessing. procps added to .reaper.toml [run] so the gate exercises the group/ownership logic rather than skipping it.
so_what: A stop command that can report success without stopping anything is the worst failure mode for an auto-restarting supervisor -- it would have made the healthcheck's restarts no-ops.

title: 0.45 harvest measured correctly on run #103: 544/544 terrain_hit and 133/133 terrain_destroyed are OURS, at 4.1 hits per destroy, with NO pinning (worst single eid+tile pair = 4 hits). But 133 destroys yielded only 8 lumber `drop` events (~6%).
detail: Attribution correction that invalidates earlier event-count reads: `eid` (numeric entity id) and `char_uid` (string) are DIFFERENT namespaces, so filtering events by char_uid-in-roster matches nothing. Our eids come from frames[].chars[].eid; our deaths are death payloads with kind_name=='char' AND guild_id in ours. Rivals harvest too -- run #100 (no harvest code) logged 187 hits / 46 destroys, none ours.
so_what: Slice 2 must measure material STOCK, not destroy counts: the destroy->drop conversion is the open question, and a tool (axe/pickaxe) may be what changes it.

title: Run #103's 5 our-char deaths (0.175/1k) are the OUTAGE, not the harvest mechanic: 4 of 5 never hit terrain, the 5th last chopped 652 ticks before dying, 12 chars harvested with 1 death -- and all 5 fall inside the final ~1200 ticks, the reconnect storm before the services went down.
detail: Control comparison: run #100 (0.42) 1 death / 0.019 per 1k frames. Do not read #103's rate as a 0.45 regression; the clean 0.45 window starts with run #113 under the new supervisor.
so_what: Judge 0.45's safety on #113, not #103.

title: ui/server.py's esc() only stringifies, and its ~46 call sites are a MIX of innerHTML template strings (which need escaping) and textContent (where escaping would render a literal &).
detail: Added escHtml() and used it in the new nav tab only. Splitting the existing call sites by context is its own change. Game-authored strings (item and mob names, and the game is an evolving target) reach several of the innerHTML sites.
so_what: Worth a dedicated pass: audit each esc() call site, use escHtml in innerHTML contexts, drop esc where the value already goes to textContent.

title: Shipped the wishlist's top item (0.5026): a 'How nav works' tab that is DERIVED rather than written down -- rules from steemer/nav.py at request time (live DIRS/SOLID + inspect.getdoc), priority ladder from the bot's own recorded decision traces.
detail: Live: 11 rungs over 4000 sampled decisions on explorer/0.45.0 (8.5 retreat -> 8.0 attack/cornered -> 7.0 undead-near -> 5.0 village actions -> 4.0 loot -> 2.5 push-north/frontier -> 2.0 nearest-frontier -> 1.5 looted-out). Anti-drift is tested by MUTATING nav and requiring the page to follow, not by comparing to a list copied into the test.
so_what: Stated limit: a branch that never fired in the sampled window is absent, not zero -- the sample size is shown next to the ladder so that is readable.

title: Operator added the 'cross-referencing exploration matrix': a noun x verb x equipped cube, each cell scored 0..1 for plausibility-by-analogy, used to drive deliberate mechanic discovery with exploring characters.
detail: Formula score -0.176 (good_idea 0.88 x risk_to_bot 0.80 x (0.75-1/1)) purely because it is just-added (tc=1) -- the same position the CODEX tab was in when the operator directed it built anyway. risk_to_bot 0.80 is the real dock and it belongs entirely to slice 3: issuing untried actions on live characters costs turns, can lose items, and can pull aggro. Slices 1-2 (build the cube; populate the TESTED layer retroactively from actions_sent x action_errors x events; score the priors from auditable rule families) are READ-ONLY and carry zero bot risk.
so_what: The 0.45 harvest win WAS one cell of this cube (tree x attack x none), found by hand after trees sat in nav.SOLID as scenery for the whole project. Slice 1 alone yields the frontier -- high-prior cells never once tried. Awaiting an operator greenlight to build (the item as given was 'this goes on the wish list').

title: We have NEVER sent `say` -- not once in 4.3M actions. The 14 verbs we have ever sent are move, embark, attack, pickup, recruit, drop, sell, buy, equip, open, use, spend_xp, brew, smelt. Every other verb in the protocol is an untouched frontier.
detail: Counts from actions_sent: move 4,070,061 / embark 249,170 / attack 110,669 / pickup 73,915 / recruit 16,283 / drop 10,232 / sell 7,358 / buy 3,965 / equip 3,211 / open 2,948 / use 2,385 / spend_xp 1,968 / brew 474 / smelt 253. Never sent: say, cast, forge, list, buy_listing, unequip, rest, refresh. The 23 tile kinds ever seen include safe, grave, portal, chest, web and track -- nouns we have almost certainly never acted on, the same shape of blind spot as trees-in-nav.SOLID. `open` is live (2,948 sends) and `nothing_to_open` is a real error reason, so the game models openable things.
so_what: Operator's point stands and is now evidenced: a `safe` has a combination and a `portal` is the canonical speak-friend-and-enter, so `say` is a legitimate mechanic-discovery surface, not merely a chat channel. It is also the CHEAPEST experiment surface (likely no turn cost). This is the single strongest argument for the exploration matrix: the frontier is not a few odd corners, it is most of the verb axis.

title: Split the exploration matrix into (A) read-only cube+frontier and (B) the experiment arm — and corrected the tc denominator: tc counts DEPLOYS since added, not loop passes.
detail: Bundled, the item scored good 0.88 x risk 0.80: ceiling 0.528, clearing 0.5 only at tc=26. Split: (A) 0.85 x 1.00 -> ceiling 0.6375, clears 0.5 at tc=7; (B) 0.88 x 0.70 -> ceiling 0.462, never clears 0.5 at any age. The tc correction matters because this pass shipped no strategy deploy (infrastructure only, explorer/0.45.0 deliberately unbumped), so current deploy-minor is 45 not 46 and every tc printed earlier today was one too high (how-nav 0.5020 not 0.5026 -- decision unchanged).
so_what: Two structural lessons for the scoring rule: (1) bundling slices of different risk lets the risky half hold the safe half hostage -- the 'bundled' dock exists for exactly this; (2) an item whose ceiling is under 0.5 is the formula correctly saying 'this always needs an explicit override', which is the right standing answer for anything that issues untried actions on live characters.

title: Recalibrated good_idea with explicit anchors after the operator asked why their ideas scored low. Root cause was mine: a 0.07-wide scoring band straddling the eligibility line, three items misreported as 'just under 0.5' when their CEILING was under 0.5, and a systematic bias against visibility/enjoyment items.
detail: ceiling = good x risk x 0.75, so at risk 0.97 good_idea must exceed 0.687 to EVER qualify; 7 of 10 items sat in 0.65-0.72. Anchoring made it worse: how-nav appears 18x in decisions.log creeping 0.496->0.502 while only tc moved. Recalibration moved 6 up and 2 down (mean +0.026, spread 1.25x) -- discrimination, not inflation. Seven items now qualify: M3a forging 0.570, shadow-eval 0.561, magic/cast 0.551, rival-recon 0.547, band-refresh 0.523, trash-talk 0.512, player market 0.505.
so_what: Two durable rules now in wishlist.md and memory: an item whose CEILING is under 0.5 is INELIGIBLE and must be reported that way, never as 'almost'; and a scoring band narrower than the decision it drives is not a measurement. Also: the recalibrated top item (M3a forging) is where the operator-directed forge-to-arm thread was already going -- the formula and the operator's judgement now agree.

title: The yield question answered: 0.45's harvest WORKS (282 trees, lumber reaches inventories) but run #113 SOLD 189 lumber, 4 ore and 2 INGOTS — the forge chain was being dismantled by the sell policy.
detail: Stock sawtooths 17->28->17->4->2->14->24->2->18 across 20,545 ticks; 244 chosen decisions read 'selling lumber (tier 1) to bank gold'. Also settles the drop-event puzzle: only 17 `drop` events for far more lumber in hand, so `drop` under-reports and STOCK is the right oracle, not events. 11 smelts produced ingots and 2 were then sold.
so_what: Slice 2 as planned ('seek more resources') would have poured material through an open door and measured as success. Fix the leak before widening the pipe. Generalises: when a chain spans two subsystems, measure the STOCK between them, not the throughput of either end.

title: 0.46.0 reserves forge feedstock (lumber/ingot/flux/plank/timber) from the sell policy, bounded at 4 per KIND per character so it cannot re-create the v0.19.0 carry clog.
detail: Branch inserted BEFORE `_should_sell`'s 'pure loot -> bank it', which was swallowing anything without recognised `uses`. Per-kind rather than a shared budget so lumber cannot crowd out ingots. Ore keeps its own smelt-pair rule ahead of the new branch. 10 tests, 6 mutants all killed.
so_what: Watch on #114: lumber/ingot sale events -> ~0, stock holds a floor, and carry-`full`/move_failed must NOT rise. Advances the top wishlist item (M3a forging 0.5707), whose only remaining blocker is now the undiscovered forge product name.

title: A mutation survivor caught a tautological test of my own: the feedstock prefix-coverage test iterated FORGE_FEEDSTOCK_PREFIXES to check FORGE_FEEDSTOCK_PREFIXES, so narrowing the tuple to ('lumber',) passed it.
detail: Rewritten to name the required kinds (lumber, ingot_copper, flux) independently in the test file, so the deliberate duplication is the check. This is the 'test against the source, not a re-export' rule catching a live instance.
so_what: Any test that loops over the constant it is validating is this bug. Mutation testing is what surfaced it -- the test passed happily for its whole (short) life before being mutated.

title: THE FORGE PRODUCT NAME — deferred since docs/07 as unpublished — was in our own events table all along: 189 `forged`/`forge_started` events from a rival name the products explicitly.
detail: forge_started payload: {"kind":"forge_started","eid":111263,"product":"shield_iron","pos":[0,0],"ticks":14} -- so forging is a 14-tick timed command and `product` is a plain kind name. Observed: shield_iron 64, dagger 47, spear 25, sickle 19, hook_chain 11, shortsword 10, pickaxe 6, pike 5, bow 2, all from one rival smith (eid 111263). Cross-referenced against live shop stock: shield_iron, hook_chain and pike are NOT SOLD -- forging is the only route, matching docs/07 on armor being unbuyable.
so_what: M3a forging (top wishlist item, 0.5707) is no longer blocked on discovery. The blocker is now ORE: we hold no ingots and almost no ore, because HARVEST_KINDS includes `vein` but adjacency-only means we break one only by luck. Seek veins.

title: Operator's observation confirmed and quantified: rival guild g_63837f keeps a mean pairwise distance of 4.06 (median 3.60, min 1.0) while we keep 22-25 — at the SAME roster size per map (4.3 vs 4.7), so it is policy on both sides, not roster size.
detail: 4000 track samples vs 370/388 of our frames. Our minimum across 370 samples was 7.0 -- our frontier-seeking never once let characters near each other. Gear is the sharper gap though: rival observations are ~60% spear|smith_apron, ours 68% None|None with 0% armor. Rival character names are ROLES: Barbarian, Harvester, Kamikaze, Miner, Ranger.
so_what: Formation is a real difference but downstream of gear; chasing it first would treat a symptom. The decisive unknown before ever copying it: is XP per-participant or SPLIT per kill? If split, grouping is actively worse for leveling and the whole argument collapses.

title: 0.46's unconditional lumber reserve was a regression I shipped and caught within the hour: it stockpiled shafts with no metal to forge them onto while cutting our main income, with gold at 139 under the 150 arm floor.
detail: 0.47 makes it conditional -- lumber/plank/timber reserved only when the character holds an ingot or an ore PAIR that can still smelt. A lone ore does not count because it can never smelt. Ingots and flux stay unconditional.
so_what: General lesson: a reserve that feeds a downstream step must be gated on that step being POSSIBLE, or it is just a leak with better branding. Check the whole chain is runnable before hoarding for its input.

title: We now buy ARMOR. In 114 runs we had bought for exactly one of five equipment slots, because the shop buy was gated on WEAPON_KINDS and on `hand` being empty -- 0% of our characters wore armor while rivals field ~60% armored.
detail: shield_wood 25g, no stat requirement, and every character has an empty offhand. The shop reports no slot (every `slot` field null), so the buy reuses what equipping LEARNED (slot_wrong/wont_fit) and refuses a kind with no empty slot left -- the guard that prevents a forever re-buy. ARMOR_BUY_FLOOR=200 > WEAPON_BUY_FLOOR=150 so arming a bare char always outranks armoring an equipped one.
so_what: Watch on #115: armor buys > 0, armored-fraction climbing, gold recovering above 150. Our own module docstring had flagged '0 with armor' long before and never acted on it -- a reminder to grep our own docstrings for known-unfixed observations.

title: XP is SPLIT across participants, not awarded per-participant in full — confirmed by two independent oracles, with a floor of ~1 xp per participant.
detail: Oracle 1 (within-character, 16 chars with both solo and shared kills, holding level/gear fixed): median shared/solo ratio 0.545 vs a split prediction of 0.47 and per-participant 1.00. Oracle 2 (total paid per kill): 5.70 at 1 participant, 5.87 at 2, 8.85 at 3 -- flat, where per-participant predicts 11.40 and 17.10. Flat within 12 mob kinds individually. The tiny-xp mobs invert (chicken 1.00->2.00, turtle 1.36->2.00), consistent with a per-participant minimum of 1.
so_what: Grouping does not MULTIPLY xp. But paired with the ~2x kill speed it produces, xp per character per unit time is roughly unchanged -- so split xp is not an argument against grouping. The case for cohesion is survivability, which then buys access to content worth more xp.

title: Ganging up roughly DOUBLES damage output while the party's incoming damage per tick stays FLAT — a mob swings at one target per tick — so per-member damage taken halves. ~2x kill speed at ~half personal damage.
detail: DPS on the mob 2.36 (1p) -> 4.80 (2p), holding within kind: rat_grey 1.86->6.07, wolf 3.78->10.42, lava_ant 2.80->9.13, skunk 2.59->5.97, mole 0.99->2.23. Party intake/tick 0.51 -> 0.49 (flat); per-member 0.51 -> 0.24. The intake result is pure geometry and cannot be confounded by rivals' better gear, unlike the DPS column.
so_what: Operator caught that I had measured xp per KILL and treated survival as a footnote -- survival is the whole case. Net ~4x less damage taken per member per kill, which is what unlocks harder content.

title: METHOD TRAP: comparing time-to-kill by participant count reads BACKWARDS. A fight only acquires a second attacker if it lasted long enough for one to arrive, so it measures 'long fights attract help', the reverse of the causal claim.
detail: My first cut showed TTK RISING with participants (bat_brown 6->16, mole 10->28, turtle 7->17) and would have 'disproved' a mechanism that is in fact real. Rate-based measures (damage per tick dealt and taken, computed only over the window in which all participants are engaged) are immune and showed the true ~2x effect.
so_what: Whenever the grouping variable is itself time-dependent, compare RATES, not durations or per-event totals. Applies to any future analysis keyed on 'how many characters were involved'.

title: Split 'Adaptive cohesion / raids' out of the Campaign Layer (0.539, qualifies). The campaign layer scored good_idea 0.80 — never the problem — but risk_to_bot 0.50 gave it a CEILING of 0.300, permanently ineligible, and it appeared in only 4 of 20 wishlist tables.
detail: The 0.50 was earned by the per-char A/B harness running divergent policies on live characters; the raids half is a term on the existing scoring ladder and carries almost none of it. Split inherits add_minor=13 so the clock is not reset. Remainder scores 0.80 x 0.55 = ceiling 0.330, ineligible, and honestly so.
so_what: I wrote 'never bundle slices of different risk' into memory the same morning (the exploration-matrix lesson) and then scored the campaign layer as a bundle anyway in the very rescore that fixed everything else. The rule needs applying to the OLD items on the list, not just the newest one -- re-examine every bundled entry, not only the one that prompted the rule.

title: 0.47's armor buy never fired on run #115: gold sits at 139 and peaks ~165 against ARMOR_BUY_FLOOR=200. The branch is correct but starved — and the sink is club churn, 14 clubs on #115 and 31 on #114.
detail: What DID work: lumber sales recovered 0.41 -> 2.66 per 1k frames (conditional feedstock reserve doing its job), armed(hand) fraction 22% -> 40%, and the equip step placed gear into offhand/outfit/trinket/boots for the first time (9 non-hand equips vs 0 on #114) -- so looted armor now gets worn even though bought armor never happens.
so_what: Lowering the floor would not help while gold cannot reach it either way. The real lever is the gold sink: recruits keep arriving bare and we keep paying 15g per club to arm them. That single sink is starving BOTH the armor buy and the forge chain.

title: 0.48.0 ships adaptive cohesion: a STANDING leash in dangerous worlds (score 2.8, above frontier and strictly below predator-spacing), gated on a new max-over-TTL per-world danger reading that counts melee predators as well as undead.
detail: Two design traps found while building. (1) The danger reading must be MAX within THREAT_TTL, not the instantaneous view -- overwritten every tick, a character seeing a quiet frame resets the world to 'safe' and a standing formation becomes impossible by construction; the feature would have shipped inert. (2) The obvious gate, the pre-existing `_world_threat`, counts UNDEAD only and reads ~0 in the mines, whose bats/rats/moles/delvers are melee predators -- gating on it would have left us dispersed in exactly the world we most want to raid.
so_what: Falsification stated before deploy: pairwise distance falls in mines/spire but NOT vale; deaths do not rise; damage taken per kill falls; move_failed does not rise (the oscillation tell); vale gathering per 1k unchanged.

title: Two mutation survivors exposed test defects of mine: a wiring test whose expected direction was ALSO produced by the frontier push, and a lone-character test that only asserted 'does not crash'.
detail: The cohesion wiring tests originally placed the ally NORTH -- but 'pushing north into unexplored ground' is scored 2.5 and moves north too, so a passing test proved nothing about cohesion. Moving the ally WEST makes the direction unambiguous, since nothing else in the ladder sends an idle character west. Separately, a mutant that let a character count ITSELF as an ally (gap 0, cohesion never fires) sailed through a test that only checked for absence of a crash.
so_what: When asserting on a chosen ACTION, pick a case no other branch in the ladder can produce -- otherwise the test passes for the wrong reason. And 'does not crash' is never sufficient for a behavioural claim.

title: Shipped the shadow-eval gate (steemer/shadow.py): replay the working tree's strategy over recorded frames and diff it against what the incumbent ACTUALLY chose. Headline output is the INERT list — branches offered many times and chosen zero times.
detail: The incumbent needs no git gymnastics: its per-tick reasoning is already in the `decisions` table. Verified cohesion on 2500 real vale frames (loot-near-ally 220 offered / 84 chosen; standalone 238 / 43) without waiting for a live dangerous band. MISUSE WARNING baked into the docstring: never diff two different live runs -- the incumbent tally must come from the SAME frames, or world variation is reported as code change.
so_what: A green suite proves code does what it says; it cannot prove behaviour ever WINS a tick, which depends on the rest of the scoring ladder and on what the world offers. That is a question only real frames answer.

title: The mutation harness could SILENTLY LIE: restoring a mutated source with shutil.move gave the file the backup's mtime — older than the .pyc built from the mutant — so CPython served the MUTANT's bytecode to later runs.
detail: Symptom: the source visibly read `if live:` while behaviour was unmistakably `if True:`. Consecutive mutants in one run could report each other's results. It survived a whole session BECAUSE the harness was rewritten ad hoc in scratch each time instead of living in the repo. Now tools/mutate.py: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, __pycache__ cleared per mutant, -p no:cacheprovider, os.utime on restore. All 21 mutants from the session re-run under the fix: all killed.
so_what: A tool whose entire job is to prove your tests CAN fail is worthless if it can lie about which code ran. Verification tooling belongs in the repo with its own tests -- including one that drives it to report a SURVIVOR, since a harness only ever observed reporting KILLED tells you nothing.

title: I wrongly called v0.48.0's cohesion INERT. Measured 'offered 28, chosen 0' ~130 ticks after deploy; over the full run #116 it was offered 688 and CHOSEN 349, first winning at tick 461.
detail: The sample sat inside the warm-up period I had documented myself minutes earlier: a redeploy resets the strategy object, so a branch gated on LEARNED state cannot fire until that state exists. v0.48.1 was shipped on that false premise; it stands on its own merits but the justification was wrong.
so_what: Encoded as shadow.MIN_DECISIONS: the gate now REFUSES to rule below a sample that could outlast a warm-up. An INERT verdict from a short window reads as evidence when it is only ignorance -- worse than no verdict at all.

title: Two promising leads dissolved on checking: the 65-70% rest rate is the game's DESIGNED pacing, and the 124 'recalled' events are almost all rivals.
detail: docs/04: 'Stamina paces the game to roughly one meaningful action per character every 4-5 ticks' => 75-80% rest is expected; we are slightly ahead of it. And the recalled char_uids are g_63837f_* (the rival guild), not our g_cd0e2a_*; run #117 has exactly 1, at 0.03 per 1k frames.
so_what: Both looked like major bottlenecks from the data alone. Read the game docs before treating a striking number as a defect -- and always check whether an event stream is about US before counting it.

title: The 'gold sink' was a BUG, not a policy: 11 of 31 buys on run #117 were duplicates within 60 ticks — one character bought SIX clubs exactly VILLAGE_ACTION_COOLDOWN apart. ~165 gold/run, against a treasury that hovers at 145 and needs 200 to buy armor.
detail: A timer is the wrong termination condition for 'has my purchase landed?': when the frame is staler than the cooldown, the char still looks bare when it expires. 0.49.0 latches the INTENT and clears it on OBSERVATION (kind in inventory or already equipped; an equipped item leaves the inventory) or on explicit REJECTION, with a TTL only as a safety net. Verified over the same frames: live 31 buys/11 dups vs candidate 3 buys/0 dups.
so_what: This is a large part of why the armor buy shipped in 0.47 never fired. Watch #118: duplicates ~0, gold climbing past 200, armored fraction finally off 0%. General lesson: when a guard exists to stop a re-send, its termination condition must be an OBSERVATION, never elapsed time.

title: Shadow-eval's real limit, found on its first use: TRUST THE STRUCTURE, NOT THE COUNTS. Replay cannot reproduce live counts because the recorded frames came from a different action sequence than the candidate would produce.
detail: Its first run also exposed a bug in its own CLI -- it replayed the OLDEST frames in the whole database against the incumbent's NEWEST decisions (storage.read_frames has no run filter), the exact misuse the docstring warns about, caught only because rest 14179->7785 was obvious nonsense. Fixed with frames_of_run(). For a change that REMOVES actions rather than adding a branch, the generic diff is the wrong instrument: count the specific thing.
so_what: new_branches / dropped_branches / inert are meaningful; `shifted` says something moved, never how much. A tool's first real use is when its assumptions get tested -- run it on a change whose answer you already know.

title: Both recent deaths had ONE cause: a tile was learn-blocked whenever a character's position merely LOOKED unchanged after a move. Frames are stale, so three in a row sealed every exit and the character rested to death at FULL stamina.
detail: Recruit-15469 (vale, tick 1413613): move S/E/W at ticks 1413599-1413601 each looked unlanded, blacklisting (7,35),(8,36),(6,36) for STUCK_BLOCK_TTL=150 with a crab_green on the fourth side; then ten consecutive ticks where `rest` (0.5) was the ONLY weighed option, hp 10->6->2, stamina 56/56. Recruit-15484 (mines) identical while burning from a drake. ZERO move_failed events and ZERO action errors in either fatal window. Fixed by driving the block from the server's `move_failed` event, which names the char and the exact tile ({'to': [5,34]}); the position-inference is deleted.
so_what: This is v0.42.0's stuck-death returning through the door that fix did not close (it excluded `not_enough_stamina` specifically; the no-error-at-all path still blacklisted). GENERAL RULE: never infer a failure from ABSENCE of a change when the observation channel is stale. Require positive evidence.

title: Operator added an expectation/reality mismatch detector: the bot declares 'we expect <foo>', a verifier follows the trail against later frames, and mismatches raise an alert surfaced in the Decisions tab.
detail: It would have caught BOTH deaths above (the expectation 'after move S my position becomes (7,35)' was violated three ticks running with nothing watching) AND the duplicate-spend bug, and it generalises v0.49.0's intent latch plus v0.50.0's evidence rule. Scored 0.90 x 0.95, ceiling 0.641, clears 0.5 at tc=7. Design trap noted in the entry: frames are stale, so predictions need a grace window or the detector repeats the exact bug it exists to catch.
so_what: Pairs with shadow.py: shadow answers 'does this branch ever WIN a tick', this answers 'when it wins, does what it expected actually happen'. It is the only item on the list that surfaces unknown-unknown misbehaviour rather than a bug already suspected.

title: 0.50.0's learned-block fix cut pathological entombment by 93%: 15.69 -> 6.48 -> 1.15 per 1k frames across runs #117/#118/#119, and the full-stamina bucket (the exact state both dead characters were in) is now EMPTY.
detail: Only visible with a refined metric. The crude 'hurt and only rest offered' signature barely moved (58.1% -> 50.3% -> 51.9%) because it counts legitimately stamina-blocked ticks. Restricting to hurt AND only-rest AND stamina>=30 (it could actually have moved) separates the pathological case from the legitimate one.
so_what: A metric that lumps a legitimate cause in with the pathological one can hide a 93% win entirely. When measuring 'the bot did nothing', always separate 'could not act' from 'could have acted and was offered nothing'.

title: v0.49's intent latch regressed on run #119 — 15 duplicate buys, 15 of 15 preceded by `not_in_village`. The rule 'an explicit rejection frees the character immediately' was too broad.
detail: The character had left the village while the stale frame still showed it there, so clearing the latch re-issued an identical buy that failed identically -- a retry storm on a PERSISTENT condition. It only surfaced because v0.50.0 unblocked movement, taking not_in_village from 8.6 to 47.6 per 1k frames. v0.50.1: only a rejection whose RETRY WOULD DIFFER (wrong_slot, stat_requirement) frees the latch; the rest wait out INTENT_TTL.
so_what: Two lessons. (1) Classify rejections by whether retrying changes anything -- a persistent rejection plus an immediate retry is a storm. (2) A fix in one subsystem can expose a latent bug in another by changing the error MIX; re-measure the things you already 'fixed' after any change that shifts behaviour upstream.

title: Why regressions kept shipping past a green, fully mutation-killed gate: every one lived in an input nobody ENUMERATED. Mutation testing proves a test is SENSITIVE to code changes; it cannot prove the tests COVER the input space.
detail: v0.46.0's space was (has lumber, has metal) and only the lumber axis was tested; v0.49.0's was 17 distinct `reason` values and two were tested, one of them classified wrong. Live data caught all three, a run later, never the gate. Countermeasure: steemer/vocabulary.py harvests the real vocabularies from history into a frozen fixture, and property tests run over ALL of them -- verified by restoring v0.49's clause, which the new test kills.
so_what: AND enumeration is only half. Asserting behaviour == the constant under test is derived from that constant, so a WRONG classification survived; the 17 reasons are now also partitioned BY HAND. Enumeration catches 'the code ignores the rule'; deliberate duplication catches 'the rule is wrong'.

title: Exploration matrix (A) shipped: over 9,100 cells it reports SIX frontier cells, topped by `lumber x forge` at 0.95 — independently surfacing the M3a blocker and the operator's magic-word intuition from a standing rule.
detail: Read-only. Priors from auditable rule families rather than per-cell guesses, so a noun the game invents tomorrow is scored on appearance. Tested layer recovered retroactively from actions_sent x action_errors. Frontier: chest/grave/portal/safe/wall x say at 0.70, and 12 of the 26 protocol verbs have never been sent at all.
so_what: The single highest-plausibility untried cell in the whole cube is the same thing the wishlist independently ranks first (M3a forging 0.573). Two independent methods agreeing on the next lever is the strongest signal either could give.

title: The 4.5% frame loss is OURS, not the server's: across a gap the next frame arrives in a median of 9ms, so messages are DISCARDED not delayed — and 34% of our frames take longer than the ~83ms production budget to handle (worst 2,972ms).
detail: A ZeroMQ DEALER drops rather than blocks when its send queue fills, so our processing stalls cost 31 gaps averaging 131 frames on run #120. The bot then commanded characters that had moved on: unknown_character 1.1 -> 104 per 1k frames, error rate 12.7% -> 42.9%. Connection stable throughout (no reconnect, silence or kick between gaps).
so_what: Re-prices the wishlist item 'move the storage mirror off the decision hot path' (0.344, marked INELIGIBLE with 'revisit if frame staleness ever proves material'). It proved material.

title: Three of my own measurement errors in one diagnosis: 'fielded collapsed 10->6' (artifact of reading chars_by_world, which is empty in field frames), 'recruits spiked to 110' (duration, not rate), and 'all gaps in vale therefore server-side' (seq is GLOBAL and round-robins worlds) — the last of which I had already FILED as a server bug.
detail: Retracted in server_bugs.md before anyone acted on it. The authoritative portal (/api/spectate/guilds) showed the roster stable at 10 the whole time; the operator had to point me at it.
so_what: When a metric is surprising, check the SOURCE's semantics before believing it -- and prefer the authoritative endpoint over a derived field. Never file a report against a third party on an unverified assumption.

title: 0.51.0 moved storage writes to a worker thread and SEGFAULTED the live bot (exit 139, zero frames across runs #124-126). The MariaDB connection is also used from the main thread by begin_run/end_run/flush, and mysql-connector is not safe for that.
detail: Eight tests and eight killed mutants -- all correct in isolation. I checked whether other THREADS touched storage and found none; the right question was OWNERSHIP of the connection, and the lifecycle callers were the input I never enumerated. Reverted in 0.51.1, keeping the thread-free half (decide+send before record). A test pins run() against constructing an _AsyncMirror.
so_what: Re-enable only when the writer owns its own connection. And note the shape: yet another regression living in an input (a caller) that was never enumerated -- the session's recurring failure mode.

title: FORGE recipes learned from the server's own rejections on run #129: spear = 1 ingot + 1 lumber, dagger = 1 + 1, shield_iron = 3 ingots + 1 lumber (2+2 and every cheaper combination refused with wrong_materials).
detail: The `product` name was never unpublished -- 189 rival forged/forge_started events in our own DB name it outright. All five `forged` events on #129 were ours (spear x2, dagger x2, shield_iron x1) from 15 forge actions, 6 wrong_materials and 2 no_forge_nearby. Quantities remain undocumented, so the ladder blacklists each rejected (product, ingots, lumber).
so_what: The M3a chain is closed end to end: harvest -> smelt -> forge. An action_error is the documentation. ORE is now the bottleneck -- 491 trees destroyed vs 6 veins on run #128.

title: Forging was value-DESTROYING: run #129 forged five items and sold every one of them (spear, dagger, shield_iron all appear in the `sale` feed under our own guild_id).
detail: Entirely mechanical and NOT a 0.52 regression. _equip_action filled only EMPTY slots, so the brute-force slot search tried the forged spear in outfit/trinket/boots and learned all three were wrong_slot (20 of 20 equip errors). That left `hand`, holding a 15-gold club, and _should_sell keeps gear 'only while a slot it could still go into remains'. The sell rule long predates the forge; 0.52 merely made the first items that ever met it. Fixed in 0.53.0 by letting gear displace strictly dearer same-class gear, ranked on the shop's own buy_price.
so_what: Shipping a producer without checking what CONSUMES its output can be worse than not shipping it. Verify the whole chain, not the new link. Named gap: shield_iron has no shop price, so it can only be worn into an empty offhand -- valuing the unbuyable is the next slice.

title: The mutation harness reported KILLED for two mutants whose test names DID NOT EXIST -- it infers 'killed' from a nonzero pytest exit, and pytest also exits nonzero when the selector matches nothing.
detail: Second time this harness has silently lied in one session (the first was the bytecode-mtime trap). It now runs each selector clean BEFORE mutating and refuses to score it unless it passes unmutated. Verified by feeding it a deliberately nonexistent selector, which it now SKIPs rather than scoring.
so_what: A check that cannot fail is indistinguishable from a passing suite. Self-test the oracle: feed it the output a broken system would produce and confirm it complains. Both failures here were in the oracle, not the code.

title: The frame-loss fix needed no worker thread: 0.51.1's reorder alone took run #128 to 85,319 frames with 0 gaps and 0.0% loss, against #120's 3.7% across 31 gaps.
detail: >200ms stalls fell 11.6% -> 2.1%; unknown_character 136.3 -> 5.3/1k, no_such_character 67.0 -> 4.5, not_in_village 153.2 -> 33.7. The elaborate version (0.51.0) segfaulted the bot; the free half was the entire fix.
so_what: The 'move the storage mirror off the hot path' wishlist item is closed by MEASUREMENT rather than by building it. Do not rebuild the async mirror -- there is no remaining latency problem for it to solve.

title: CONFIRMED LIVE: the server ACCEPTS equipping into an already-occupied slot. Run #130 frame 4559057 shows char c15829's `hand` changing in place from club -> dagger (non-empty to non-empty), and the displaced clubs were then sold.
detail: This was genuinely unknown when 0.53.0 shipped -- undocumented, untestable offline, and hedged with SWAP_GIVE_UP=3 in case no such mechanic existed. It does. Two oracles: the decision was issued ('upgrading hand: dagger (20g) over club (15g)') AND the equipment map changed in place across frames. Zero swap refusals; the only equip errors on the run are 11 wrong_slot, which route to the slot map by design. Gear sales on #130 are clubs ONLY (x5) -- displaced items banked, nothing crafted sold, against #129 which sold spear, dagger and shield_iron.
so_what: The gear ladder now closes end to end: forge or loot something better -> displace the worse item -> sell the displacement. c15829 is wearing a FORGED shield_iron in its offhand, which the shop sells at no price and we could not otherwise own.

title: v0.54.0 vein-seek shipped INERT: 0 firings in 7,714 frames. I validated it against the tiles_seen TABLE's accumulated 85-vein map, but bot.known starts EMPTY every run and tiles_seen had no reader.
detail: Not outscored -- never offered, against 1,024 adjacent-harvest offers in the same window. Run #130 saw 2 unique vein positions across 32k frames while the database knew 85. Fixed by hydrating the map at startup (0.55.0).
so_what: Validating a behaviour against data the RUNNING system does not have proves nothing. Same failure shape as the 0.51.0 segfault, where the un-enumerated input was a caller rather than a data source. Check what the process actually holds in memory, not what the database holds.

title: Hydrating the map 4x'd move failures (5.2% -> 19.4% of moves) because every field goal search was UNBOUNDED -- chest-beelining became a cross-map pilgrimage at 1.6 decisions per frame.
detail: Unboundedness had been harmless only by accident: pre-hydration a character knew a few hundred tiles, so the nearest chest was necessarily near and usually had no known corridor to it. Scoping WHICH chests count (0.56.0) recovered almost nothing because the survivors were still reachable from anywhere. Bounding errands to FIELD_GOAL_RANGE=20 (0.57.0) took move failures to 1.5% -- below the pre-hydration baseline -- restored chest-beelining to 0.046/frame against 0.047 before, and left harvest running ~7x the old rate.
so_what: When you widen what a system KNOWS, re-check every consumer that derives targets from that knowledge. A limit that was never written down, but was enforced by the old data's smallness, disappears silently.

title: The full suite passed with a change that would have stranded hurt characters mid-retreat -- nothing pinned the retreat's need for UNBOUNDED range.
detail: _retreat walks home via the shared _step helper (goal y==0) and characters range to y=126 in mines, y=199 in vale. Applying the new errand bound to it would leave a hurt character unable to find a route and offering `rest` instead: precisely the stuck-death of v0.42.0/v0.50.0. Caught by reading the call sites, not by the suite. A test now walks a character home from 100 tiles out and the mutant that removes the exemption dies against it.
so_what: A green suite is evidence about what is TESTED, not about what is safe. When adding a constraint to a shared helper, enumerate its callers and ask which of them the constraint must not reach -- and note that the survival paths are exactly the ones least likely to have a unit test.

title: Brewing had been dead for want of a 2-gold item: `bottle_empty` had NO acquisition path anywhere in the strategy (it appeared only in KEEP and in the brew gate's counter), so when found bottles ran out, brewing stopped -- 0 brews in 31,011 frames.
detail: This silently invalidated v0.35.0's reasoning for raising POTION_RESERVE 100 -> 600, which was explicitly premised on heals being 99.6% free-brewed. With brewing dead and the buy gated at 600 against 183 actual gold, 0.0% of characters carried a potion_red. Buying bottles (0.58.0) restored it immediately: 2 bottles -> 2 brews on run #135, including an undecoded learning batch that taught bitterroot -> potion_purple.
so_what: When a decision is justified by 'X supplies this for free', something must guarantee X keeps working. Here nothing did, and the failure was invisible because the fallback existed -- it was simply gated out of reach. Check the SUPPLY of anything a reserve or threshold depends on.

title: The ore bottleneck is DEPTH, not seeking: characters sit at median depth y=2 (p90 6) while the shallowest vein is y=26 and the median vein is y=88. Only 1.0% of mines char-frames are within vein-seek's 14-tile range.
detail: Across 31,011 frames on run #134, vein-seek fired 751 times in streaks averaging 15 ticks and NO character was ever adjacent to a vein. POISON_SAFE_DEPTH=12 caps any character without a potion_red, and 0.0% carried one.
so_what: Three passes of ore work (0.45 harvest, 0.54 seek, 0.55 map memory) were all downstream of a cap nobody had connected to ore. Before optimising a behaviour that is firing but not converting, check whether the WORLD it needs is reachable at all -- measure the gap between where characters are and where the target is.

title: A BAND REFRESH collapsed ground loot 18x (1.06 -> 0.06 visible items per frame) and idled the entire economy: no loot -> nothing carried -> nothing sold -> gold frozen at 138, below the 150 arm floor, so no buys, no bottles, no brewing.
detail: Run #136 sent ONLY move and embark, where a matched 8,000-tick window of #135 had attack/pickup/sell/buy/brew/forge. Deaths also went 83 -> 0. The frame carries `next_refresh: {band, in_ticks}` and the refresh lands at tick 1574878, right at the run boundary. We ignore that field entirely.
so_what: A starving band is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a broken bot in our metrics -- it cost this pass its measurement and nearly cost a good change a false rollback. This is the concrete argument for the band-refresh wishlist item: read `next_refresh`, and never attribute an economy metric across a refresh boundary.

title: I called run #136's collapse a 0.59.0 regression. It was not: replaying the SAME 400 real frames through 0.58.0 and 0.59.0 produced byte-identical actions (move 455, embark 55).
detail: The offline probe never reproduced field opportunism at all, so its output was a property of the PROBE, not of the change. Reading the code would also have said so -- _should_sell is only reachable from village(), so the field actions it appeared to break were never downstream of it.
so_what: Before attributing a live change to a code change, run the OLD code against the SAME input. A probe that cannot reproduce the baseline behaviour cannot testify about a regression in it -- establish that a harness reproduces the phenomenon before trusting it to detect a change in it.

title: Band refreshes are detectable from `next_refresh: {band, in_ticks}`: the band number changes OR in_ticks jumps up (a countdown only falls, so a rise is a new cycle). Ten boundaries in ~14,000 ticks, each world on its own schedule.
detail: A refresh REFILLS chests -- `chest` sightings spike to 424 in the loot-rich bucket against 14-80 elsewhere -- and swings ground loot ~900x within a single run (0.052 -> 1.839 -> 0.002 visible items/frame). 0.60.0 revives emptied chests as targets on a refresh, keeping the hypothesis OUT of the observed map.
so_what: Never attribute an economy metric across a refresh boundary; the same run can look dead and healthy 20 minutes apart. The signal was in every field frame all along.

title: I sized a blind spot by counting SIGHTINGS instead of distinct tiles: '2,500-4,600 chest_open sightings per bucket' is repeated views of the same few tiles. The real population is 22 distinct emptied chests (mines 11, vale 10, spire 1).
detail: Stated in the 0.60.0 commit message before I checked tiles_seen for distinct counts. A 20k-frame replay confirmed the true scale: 12 chest-reviving refreshes but a peak of only 2 simultaneous recheck targets. The change is still correct and cheap; it is a modest lever, not a large one.
so_what: Sighting-count and distinct-count answer different questions, and the frame stream makes the former trivially large. Before sizing an opportunity from event volume, collapse to the distinct entities involved -- GROUP BY the identity, not the observation.

title: 90% of our pickups fail silently: `pickup` confirms 90 times against 811 violations across 20,000 frames. `overburdened` fires 1,164 times against 283 real pickup events -- and the server reports it as an EVENT, not an action_error, so every error query came back clean.
detail: The strategy's shed-when-overburdened logic keys off `carry.used >= cap`, which is NEVER true (0 of 8,200 char-frames within 2 of the cap). `overburdened` means 'this ITEM does not fit' by BULK, not 'the pack is full'. So a character re-issues a doomed pickup and nothing learns from the refusal -- the same shape as the pre-0.50.0 learned-block bug. Found by the v0.61.0 expectation detector on its first run over real data.
so_what: NEXT LEVER: learn from `overburdened` (shed by bulk, or stop re-issuing for that item). Also a general lesson: the server signals refusal through TWO channels -- action_errors AND events -- and we had only ever watched one.

title: An aggregate violation-rate alarm would have been decorative: `move` resolved 29,779 times against `pickup`'s 901, so a pickup failing nine times in ten came to 2.6% of the total.
detail: Corrected mid-build to alarm PER ACTION FAMILY, with a per-family minimum sample. Also caught before deploy: an alarm dict lacking `subtype` raises a KeyError inside on_frame, because GuildBot._report_anomaly reads that key -- the observability tool would have taken the bot down.
so_what: Rare-but-broken hides under common-and-healthy in any pooled rate. Alarm on the family, not the total -- and test a new emitter against its REAL consumer, not against your reading of it.

title: The server refuses through TWO channels -- action_errors AND events -- and we had only ever watched one. `overburdened` is an EVENT, so 1,164 refused pickups were invisible to every action_error query.
detail: Compounded by a units mismatch: our fullness test counts SLOTS (used >= cap-1) while capacity is spent in BULK. All 1,164 events were one character at carry (19,21) -- two slots free, unable to take a bulk-3 item, not 'full' by our rule (needs 20) and not shedding (needs 21). Fixed by trusting the refusal (TTL, scoped to our eids) and both suppressing pickup and shedding. Ground items do not expose `bulk`, so modelling it would have been a guess where the verdict is a fact.
so_what: When an action fails silently, check the EVENT stream as well as action_errors. And beware guards written in different units from the constraint they approximate -- slots vs bulk left a gap that no single threshold covered.

title: Third time mutation testing caught me sizing a test fixture FROM the constant under test (VEIN_SEEK_RANGE, SCARCE_LONE_KEEP, OVERBURDENED_TTL). It is a habit, not three accidents.
detail: Each time the fixture moved with the mutant and the test stayed green -- e.g. shrinking OVERBURDENED_TTL to 1 while the test computed its ticks as TTL-1 and TTL. The remedy each time: hardcode the POLICY claim ('+5 ticks still refused, +500 long gone') and pin the constant's band in a separate test.
so_what: When a test needs a magnitude, never derive it from the value being tested. Write the claim in absolute terms and assert the constant sits in the band the claim assumes -- then a change that invalidates the premise fails loudly instead of going vacuous.

title: Magic was never priced out: we have SOLD 74 TOMES (ring 22, step 16, field 14, veil 13, bolt 9) for 36-44 gold apiece against a 120-150 shop price, and have never learned a single spell.
detail: A tome teaches a spell FORM by being `use`d (docs/06) but carries `use`, not `equip`, so _should_sell filed it under 'pure loot -> bank it'. Most recent sales were runs #130/#135/#137, so this was live behaviour, not history. 0.63.0 keeps a tome while the character is under its spell_cap and uses it before the sell step, with (char, kind) learn-by-rejection since INT gates which tomes a character may use.
so_what: Before concluding a mechanic is blocked on cost or supply, CHECK WHAT WE SELL. This is the fourth scarce chain input lost to the same `pure loot -> bank it` default (lumber/ingots in 0.46, bone and raw ore in 0.59, tomes now) -- the branch is a catch-all, and every mechanic we unlock adds an item it silently misfiles.

title: Cross-guild comparison, first time we have ever looked: we field the ONLY fully-armed roster on the server (10/10 vs WillMorr 9/30 and Fable 2/9) and the highest median level (7-8 vs 3 and 2) -- while rivals work at depth 29-43 (max 57) and our characters sit at median depth 2.
detail: From the spectate and track intel feeds, which had been written for months and never read back by the dashboard. WillMorr's max level is 29 against our 16, but their median of 3 across 30 characters says that is one veteran in front of a large unarmed bench. Nobody is outfitted (us 0/10, WillMorr 1/30). Gear gap: `smith_apron`.
so_what: The depth number is POISON_SAFE_DEPTH observed FROM THE OUTSIDE, with no knowledge of our own code -- independent confirmation that depth, not seeking, is the ore bottleneck. And the arming arc (0.40/0.53) turns out to have made us the best-equipped guild, which no internal metric had ever stated.

title: The forge blacklist was ratcheting itself shut: a one-strike permanent ban on `wrong_materials` had condemned ALL FIVE spear recipes and ALL FIVE shield_iron recipes -- including (spear,1,1), which produced `forged` events on runs #129 and #140.
detail: Pairing each forge action with the item kinds it spent shows identical product, kinds and quantities both succeeding and failing within one run, so the refusal is not a function of what v0.52.0 keyed on. Fixed by making a `forged` event credit the recipe that character last attempted: proven recipes are never blacklisted, unproven ones need 3 refusals, and proof retroactively clears a wrongful ban. Cause of the non-determinism is still unknown (tier is the suspect).
so_what: A permanent one-strike blacklist against a NOISY signal only ever removes options -- it is a ratchet, and it ends inert regardless of how well the mechanic works. Any learn-by-rejection loop needs a matching source of positive evidence, or a failure budget, or both.

title: A stateless replay claimed 97% of forge opportunities were missed. Artifact: it used a FRESH strategy per frame and so did not know what the live instance had learned.
detail: Re-running the whole run through ONE stateful Explorer reproduced the live action counts almost exactly (forge 18 vs 18, smelt 11 vs 11) and pointed at the blacklist as the real cause. Also discarded en route: a 'we die 6x more per character than rivals' comparison -- we observe all our own deaths but a rival's only within our vision, so their count is a lower bound with unknown coverage.
so_what: COMPARE STATEFUL THINGS STATEFULLY. A replay harness that resets learned state measures a different system than the one running. Cousin of the iter-71 rule: before blaming a change, replay the same frames through both versions.

title: Stat-gated refusals never expired although we deliberately raise stats: `spend_xp` has fired 2,151 times and our maxima went str 2->6, vit 3->8, level 6->18, yet a kind refused at str 2 stayed refused forever in all SEVEN places wont_fit is consulted -- including the sell rule, which then banks the item.
detail: Compounded by wont_fit being keyed on KIND alone and therefore global: the weakest character to try a bow decided whether anyone could wear one. Fixed by recording the stat TOTAL that was refused, so out-growing it restores the option, a second refusal raises the bar, and a weaker refusal cannot lower it. The same release was applied to _tome_failed (INT-gated). Audit completed: slot_wrong, _swap_failed, STUCK_BLOCK and price were examined and left alone with reasons.
so_what: Ask of every latch: WHAT RESTORES AN OPTION? The ones that need an answer are those whose gate is a number the system itself moves -- here, stats we spend XP to raise. A permanent refusal against a moving threshold is a ratchet.

title: I reported 0.64.0 as confirmed on a forge success rate of 35% -> 68%. Both numbers counted RIVAL forges: run #141's `forged` events included pickaxe x5 and sickle x3, products we never attempted.
detail: Filtered to our own eids the real series is 33% (#129), 26% (#140, pre-fix), 21% (#141), 17% (#143) -- flat output of 4-6 items per run and no improvement. 0.64.0 is still structurally right (a one-strike ban on a noisy signal is a ratchet) but bought no measured gain.
so_what: Event streams are WORLD-WIDE. Filtering by ownership is not a step to remember case by case -- for any event-derived metric it is the FIRST step. I had applied it correctly to deaths one pass earlier and then omitted it for forges.

title: Forge recipe knowledge died at every deploy: run #143 had ONE character spend 20 of the run's 23 forge attempts re-walking the ladder, while run #129 had already proven the answer.
detail: The character held two ingots; shield_iron needs (3,1), proven on #129, so every quantity it could afford was known-wrong before it started. Proven recipes now persist in a `learned` table and hydrate once per process, and a product with a proven quantity only ever sends that one. Only POSITIVE facts are stored -- a persisted failure would carry a wrong belief forever, since wrong_materials is non-deterministic.
so_what: Ask of anything the strategy LEARNS: does it survive a deploy? A fresh process looks identical to a knowledgeable one for the first few minutes, which is why this stayed invisible. Still in-memory-only: slot_wrong, wont_fit, _tome_failed, _swap_failed, price.

title: v0.64.0's proof rule never ran live for two versions: event parsing lived in `_field()`, village frames route straight to `strategy.village()`, and ALL `forged` events arrive on village frames.
detail: Found because 0.66.0's `learned` table stayed empty while run #144 forged two spears. This replaces the softer reading in the same-day retraction: 0.64.0 was not 'right but unmeasured', it was INERT, so the corrected success series says nothing about it. The whole suite passed before and after -- 752 tests, none asserting that a village frame's events are read, because every test drove the strategy or the monitor directly and never the routing between them.
so_what: THIRD inert shipment (0.48, 0.54, 0.64) and all three were correct code that was never reached. When a fix shows no effect, FIRST establish that it executed -- before interpreting any numbers. And test the CHAIN end to end: a break in the middle leaves both ends green.

title: Magic was locked out by our own XP policy: INT is absent from XP_PRIORITY, and INT gates which tomes a character may use plus max_mana, spell_cap and essence_cap. Run #145 kept two dropped tomes, issued `use` on both, and got `stat_requirement` five times.
detail: The rest of the chain is proven working: tomes dropped, were kept (zero sold this run against 74 historically), and `use` was issued on exactly those item_ids. 0.67.0 raises INT only for a character carrying a tome the server has ALREADY refused it -- not merely holding one, since an untried tome is a guess and survival stats are the cost. Refusal recording (0.63.0) and retry-on-growth (0.65.1) already existed, so the loop closes with no new machinery.
so_what: A mechanic can be locked by a policy that never mentions it. When a capability stays unreachable, check what the system SPENDS on -- our XP priority had no opinion about INT at all, which is not neutrality, it is a permanent no.

title: I raised two false alarms in one pass ('forging has stopped entirely', 'terrain_hit collapsed 519 -> 8') by sampling a run in its first minutes. Full-run figures were unremarkable.
detail: terrain_hit 114.6 -> 101.3 per 10k; trees destroyed 125 -> 115; forge attempts resumed. The project already encodes this lesson as shadow.MIN_DECISIONS (v0.48.0 was declared inert from 28 offers) but I applied it only to the shadow harness, not to ad-hoc queries.
so_what: A run younger than ~20k frames cannot support a claim that something STOPPED. Re-measure at full length before diagnosing -- the same haste produced a false regression diagnosis in iter 71.

title: The tome holder never went to the village: `tome_field` sat in one character's pack for all 10,933 of its tome-carrying frames, every one in vale, while the learn step lived only in village().
detail: So it never learned AND never earned the stat_requirement refusal that v0.67.0's INT investment keys on -- the chain was waiting on an event that could not occur. 0.68.0 offers the learn in the field (`use` is already how potions are drunk there), scored to fill an idle tick and never compete with survival. Verified live on #147 within minutes: 2 learn decisions, 2 use actions, 2 refusals earned.
so_what: FOURTH link in this chain that was correct and unreachable (0.54 seek, 0.64 proof rule, 0.67 INT, 0.68 learn step). Always the same shape: code that executes somewhere the subject is not. Before shipping a behaviour, name the frame it fires on and the character it fires for, and check that character gets there.

title: POTION_RESERVE=600 defended a premise that expired: v0.35.0 set it because heals were 99.6% free-brewed (4,511 drinks vs 16 buys), but across ~180,000 recent frames we brewed SEVEN potion_red and only 4.1% of char-frames carry one.
detail: The reserve also made the fallback unreachable by arithmetic -- gold runs 156-200, a potion_red costs 20, the buy needed 620. Lowered to the weapon floor: an un-healed character is capped at POISON_SAFE_DEPTH, which gates ore, deeper content and XP. Bounded by POTION_KEEP=1/char and the floor itself. One existing test asserted the opposite premise and was rewritten to what survives (a bottle is 2g against a potion's 20).
so_what: SECOND time a well-reasoned constant outlived its evidence (this, and v0.8.0's stranded-singleton rule fixed in 0.59.0). When a constant carries a justification, that justification is a CLAIM ABOUT THE WORLD -- and claims about the world expire. Nothing was watching either.

title: The map edge counted as unexplored, so 58 of the mines' 126 'frontier' tiles sat at y=0 -- and bfs_step returns the NEAREST goal, so characters at median depth 2 chased the rim forever while the real frontier (depth 89-126) and the veins (median depth 88) went untouched.
detail: Self-reinforcing: staying shallow kept the false frontier nearest, and the behaviour meant to push characters outward was the one pinning them. Fixed by plumbing the frame's `bounds` into nav.frontier, optional throughout so village frames and replays keep the old behaviour. Live effect: 572 false frontier tiles removed (mines 126->68, vale 526->12). Flagged in iter 69 and deferred as smaller; it was the binding constraint on depth.
so_what: A goal test that treats 'absent from my map' as 'unexplored' will always prefer the edge of the map. Also: removing a false attractor is not adding a true one -- the genuine frontier is outside errand range, so idle time may rise, which is the next thing to measure.

title: NEGATIVE RESULT: the 1.5x move-stamina margin is correctly calibrated and was NOT changed. Moves still fail not_enough_stamina at shown-stamina up to 29-30 (median 26-28), exactly as v0.9.0 measured.
detail: 55% of decisions are `rest` with traces reading 'wanted move but stamina 18 < ~30', which looked like a margin wasting half our ticks. Measured: a move costs ~15 and resting regenerates 10-12 per tick, so resting most ticks is inherent to the stamina economy rather than a defect.
so_what: Two constants were re-tested this week: POTION_RESERVE had expired, MOVE_STAMINA_SAFETY had not. Re-testing is worth it precisely because you cannot tell which from the comment alone -- and a negative result is worth recording so the next person does not re-litigate it.

title: 0.70.0 (bounds-aware frontier) is a clear win at comparable loot density: XP +27%, sale gold +103%, terrain broken 4x, deaths halved, and the rest share FELL 53.9% -> 47.0%.
detail: The idle rise I explicitly warned about did not happen. Removing the fake rim frontier let v0.36.0's depletion-aware world-hopping win instead: embarks and returns roughly doubled and attacks nearly tripled, so characters stopped walking the map edge and started leaving exhausted worlds. Depth p90 moved 6 -> 12.
so_what: Removing a false attractor freed an existing, better behaviour that had been losing to it. Worth checking, when a behaviour underperforms, whether something fake is out-competing it rather than assuming the behaviour is wrong.

title: The ore errand was sized never to reach the ore: veins sit at median depth 88 (shallowest 24), the median character-to-vein distance is 30, and VEIN_SEEK_RANGE was 14 -- only 4.72% of mines char-frames were ever within reach.
detail: Runs #148/#149 broke 4 and 3 veins against 44 and 193 trees. A healed character now ranges 32 tiles, chosen to clear the measured median of 30 and pinned to that measurement by a test. Gated on the heal because veins are deep and depth is where poison kills. Move-failure budget measured first: 0.24-0.33% against a 5.2% baseline.
so_what: Check that a bounded search can actually REACH its targets -- compare the bound against the measured distance distribution, not against intuition. A range chosen for safety can quietly make a behaviour ornamental.

title: Cohesion was 25% of ALL decisions and converged never: closing on the NEAREST ALLY is mutual pursuit. One character logged 482 consecutive cohesion decisions with the ally distance reading 13,9,8,7,6,8,8,6,8; four characters at one tick were all 'closing' at distance 7, two north and two south.
detail: With rest at ~47%, roughly 72% of decisions produced no progress. Cohesion (2.8) also outranks vein-seek (2.7), so a 'dangerous' world suppressed ore-seeking entirely while the chase went nowhere. Fixed by rallying to the group's CENTRE -- a fixed point for the tick, so the spread shrinks monotonically. Two clusters 40 apart now meet at the midpoint and settle.
so_what: Any 'move toward the nearest X' where X is also moving toward something is a chase, not a convergence. Rally to a point computed from the group, not to a member of it. Found only by tracing a single character's consecutive decisions -- aggregate counts showed cohesion as a normal-looking 25% slice.

title: Field stints have a MEDIAN OF 9-10 TICKS and only 1.6-3.4% last the ~60 ticks a 30-tile walk needs -- so any errand longer than a few tiles cannot complete, including the 14-tile original.
detail: Measured on runs #149 and #150, band-independent. This is why vein-seek has never converted in any version: the median char-to-vein distance is 30 and characters are recalled or diverted within ~10 ticks.
so_what: SIZE AN ERRAND AGAINST THE UNINTERRUPTED TIME AVAILABLE, not against the distance to the target. A range chosen from the target distribution alone will be ornamental if the actor never gets that long.

title: The loop's own error rate now exceeds the bot's: 6 attribution errors in 24h (11 across history), 4 correct-but-unreachable versions, 7 test-craft slips, 2 expired premises -- while a prose directive covering the first class was already in place the whole time.
detail: Fixed with five EXECUTABLE mechanisms rather than more prose: steemer/attribution.py (ours_only defaults true, TooEarly under 20k frames, compare() carries the band confounder, distinct_entities), steemer/claims.py + tools/recheck_claims.py (the expectation detector pointed at the loop's own reported numbers), and three ratcheting tests (reachability, test-hygiene, premise staleness). Budgets may only decrease; one behaviour was converted immediately to show the ratchet turning.
so_what: A directive that cannot fail does not change behaviour -- everything that ever stuck here was executable (shadow.MIN_DECISIONS, the mutate self-test, the pre-commit hook). When you catch yourself writing a rule into a document, ask what would have to fail for the rule to be enforced.

title: 0.72.0's centre-rally converged in simulation and never in play — a rally needs uninterrupted ticks, and a field stint is median 10-12 against a median centre distance of 13. Bounded at COHESION_RANGE=8, cohesion's chosen share fell 18.2%->1.02%.
evidence: Frames #150/#151: spread median 43->39, tight<=6 share 1.7%->1.3%; decision_share #151 18.17% -> #157 1.02%; tools/field_stints.py medians 10/12.
so_what: Gate any N-tick behaviour on N; also fixed the gate/step mismatch (gate measured nearest ally, step walked to centre).

title: RETRACTED: 'cohesion was 25% of all decisions' — decisions.reasoning stores the WHOLE trace; the LIKE merged CHOSEN (11.6%), offered-and-lost (+0.2), and stamina-suppressed-before-weighing (+12 points).
evidence: Run #150: 144,179 decisions; 'ally' in reasoning 23.9% vs chosen-flag share 11.6% (alternatives_json). Corrected figures in claims.jsonl iter-88.
so_what: Offered, chosen, and wanted-but-suppressed are three populations with one English name; use attribution.decision_share(chosen=...).

title: The action table's 'where' column means WHERE THE ACTION IS LEGAL: say is scoped 'map', and three village says were rejected not_in_village before the column was read right; placement then took three scores (0.6 and 1.1 fired ZERO times; 2.1 works — scout 1.0 and walk-home 1.5 are near-always available).
evidence: action_errors #154: say/not_in_village x3; #155-157: says at 2.1 sent clean, event-keyed lines live.
so_what: Check docs/03's scope column before building on a verb; 'score it below everything' = 'it will never happen'.

title: A heal potion is the PASSPORT NORTH: chars carrying one ran median y~50 (max 125); the 99.5% without were pinned at median y 0 by POISON_SAFE_DEPTH — the roster confined to the bottom 12 rows of a 199-row map.
evidence: #157 y-distributions: healed n=665 median 50; bare n=124,917 median 0 (79% at y0-9); gold 149 vs effective potion line 170 checked second: 0 bought, 0 brewed.
so_what: The heal buys map access; it now has first call on gold at floor 100, and every later depth win stacked on this.

title: After 0.70.0 removed the false frontiers, the nearest TRUE frontier sat 64-192 tiles from the spawn strips — beyond the 20-tile errand bound in every world — so no frontier offer could fire from where the roster lived.
evidence: Bounds-correct frontier scan: vale 192 / mines 86 / spire 64 tiles from strip. Trek on #159: healed median y 4->21 max 30->125, deaths 6.9->2.5/10k.
so_what: A bounded search silently deletes a behaviour class when world geometry outgrows the bound.

title: THE VAULT IS A MIRAGE: guild.inventory lists 202 potion_red + 404 bottle_empty that the server rejects no_such_item on withdrawal (8 distinct ids), while gold in the SAME dict updates live. server_bugs.md carries the repro.
evidence: #160: 1,181 withdrawals of item 13913 all rejected in 1,083 frames; #161: ids 13913..14259 x2 each rejected then fail-closed silence.
so_what: 'Harmless to retry' needs a proof for the PERMANENT case; guild.inventory is not a manifest.

title: Brewing died of one line: the bottle-buy floored at WEAPON_BUY_FLOOR=150, unreachable at the guild's actual 100-150 gold — zero bottles ever bought against a supply that once provided 99.6% of heals.
evidence: All-time actions_sent: 0 bottle buys before 0.79.0; #162 minutes after deploy: bottle -> brewed potion_red; potion_red is the all-time top brew product (137).
so_what: Audit every purchase floor against the gold the guild actually holds — correct-tested-unreachable is a failure class.

title: The live hello config does NOT carry ride_max_tiles/ride_stamina (docs list them as examples): captured tick_seconds=0.25, idle_recall=2000, refresh_warning=240, say_max=40, caps 5/10/30. The ride cap is discoverable only empirically.
evidence: learned(topic=server_config) per-key rows; the first blob write truncated at learned.fact varchar(255) in prod.
so_what: Store learned facts as key=value rows, never blobs; never assume a documented config key exists until the wire shows it.

title: The mines rails are 19 SEPARATE short lines (verticals + one 2-D junction), all 78 ends on mapped ground; the longest ride is 12 tiles along y=8 AND ENDS AT A CHEST; chest density beside track 5.0% vs 2.0%. `ride` has never been issued.
evidence: tiles_seen survey: 60 track tiles, 8-connectivity components, per-direction runs, end kinds 34 wall / 25 floor / 19 chest_open.
so_what: Value is the flat-cost strip traverse + chest runs, NOT a route north; the 'fragments of longer rails' first read was wrong on both counts.

title: Remembered terrain is only MOSTLY durable: deep trekkers' RETREATS bounced off regrown bush/rock/water 524 times (move_failed 31->231/10k) — attributed by joining each solid bounce to its issuing decision (239 of top 255 = 'looted-out, home').
evidence: #164 bounce kinds floor 660 / rock 237 / water 160 / bush 96; freshness bias STALE_COST=3 measured 231->50->39/10k across #165/#167.
so_what: Long-range routing over hydrated maps needs a freshness prior; the strip never showed it because it re-sees itself every tick.

title: TASTE — never sent in project history despite knowledge.py saying 'resolve with taste first' since run #8 — decoded four kinds in one run: bitterroot=AETHER, frostmoss=EMBER, glimmerweed=CLARITY, sungrass=FROST, refuting both run-#8 guesses.
evidence: [taste] raw event specimens in steemer-live.log; learned(topic=essence) rows; guessed parser fields matched the live shape exactly.
so_what: None is vigor (heal supply unchanged), but casting speaks the essence language — every decode stocks magic's ammunition.

title: The player market had NEVER been used by any guild — market_listings [] in every recorded frame — until our 3g lumber probe became the first listing in server history (listing_id 'L393559', per-viewer `mine` flag).
evidence: All-history frame scans of guild.market_listings; the live listing in #167+ frames; our 'listed' event specimen.
so_what: Shop pays 20% of list; any rival buy_listing triples top-volume income. Watch for the first buyer.

title: NOBODY on the server uses magic: 0 implements across ~340k roster observations of all five guilds (the dev's level-38 guild is 73% bare-handed), 0 spells held anywhere, no implements in the shop.
evidence: 6,484 spectate snapshots aggregated by guild and hand-kind; shop stock survey (tomes only: veil 120g, bolt 150g); our use->stat_requirement x40.
so_what: Magic is an uncontested combat axis; the blockers are one tome and ~24 gifted XP of INT.

title: The caster pipeline: int-GIFTED chars pre-bank INT to 6 (half cost) in parallel with saving for tome_veil; the buy waits for gold>=220 AND INT>=4 (operator: protect the wizard, don't burn gold). A tome is only CONSUMED on successful learning, so refusals are free retries and the stat-growth retry performs the INT-threshold search automatically.
detail: First INT ever banked minutes after deploy (#168); wizard role named + purple badge; permadeath makes the investment compound. Re-derive CASTER_INT_TARGET when the first use succeeds.
so_what: Watch for the learned event — the guild's first spell in server history.

title: Both #170 wizard deaths were the MOB-BOX (the operator's screenshot, with corpses): one rested SIX ticks at full stamina while eaten — retreat and desperation both empty, strike range absolute in blocked — one bounced the same doomed move 4x.
evidence: Death traces #170 ticks 2020238/2021035 (chose: rest x6 at hp 9->2; move E x4 static); the planned-escape tests reconstruct the exact geometry and now offer the southward crossing.
so_what: Danger is a price (AVOID_COST=8 ~ one eaten hit), not a wall, wherever the alternative is dying in place.

title: Formation jitter root cause (operator diagnosis, confirmed): every member computed its OWN target from the other members, and self-exclusion gave each a DIFFERENT rally point — mutual pursuit. The PARTY is now the unit: one anchor square (the arch-wizard's tile), identical for all; partied chars skip cohesion; cohesion's centroid includes self.
evidence: #174 gap series 7,7,19,6,4,4,5,5,7,6 (closes monotonically); zero traces with two formation targets; 0.85.1 had bounded a 130-tile 'escort' first.
so_what: Never compute a formation target per-character from other members' positions; shared fixed points converge.

title: The gift lottery paid immediately on the roster fill: 33 free recruits to cap delivered 4 wizards, 4 guardians, 8 foragers, 4 fodder within ten minutes; 39 pair-embarks formed parties at the village gate.
evidence: #175 actions_sent (33 recruits), village-frame role census {fodder 4, forager 8, wizard 4, guardian 4}, pair-embark traces.
so_what: Recruits are free and ~1 in 3 rolls int-gifted: the bench IS the wizard pipeline; fodder absorbs the bad dice at zero coin.

title: The doctrine's first mature run (#175) was a regression: 20 deaths (8.2/10k, 4x), NINE wizards — near home (y=2-16), escorts present — because pair-embark shipped wizards wherever a guardian stood, and an escort is not an answer to an undead band.
evidence: #175: deaths by role {wizard 9, guardian 5, forager 5, fodder 1}; death y's 2-29; bounce-tick winners = flee/no-heal-retreat offers; xp 2.0/10k; zero INT spends (wizards earned 0 XP).
so_what: 0.87.1: wizards sit out dangerous bands entirely (safe-world pair-embark, safe-world join, and walk-home on hostile refresh). An escort protects against a box, not a cycle; the pipeline waits at home. move_failed 210/10k left as a WATCH (churn composition, no formation signature).

title: The chosen six: wizardhood became a SEAT — top-6 by (INT, level, gift, stats, uid) as a PURE function of a sightings ledger, no stored state. Death = instant promotion by re-ranking; WIZARD_MIN_POOL=12 prevents restart paralysis (caught by test: 2 sighted chars both crowned themselves and walked home); seats route EVERY XP to INT uncapped to 24.
detail: Operator directive verbatim: max 6, two per map, chosen by int (tie: level, stats), max their int, demote the rest, promote on death with lowest-stat recall making room. UI runs the same pure ranking, so panel and strategy cannot disagree.
so_what: Watch: INT climb rate on the six, first tome at INT>=4 + gold>=220, the learned event = the glass ceiling breaking.

title: Run #177's move_failed 304/10k was 17k GHOST COMMANDS, not terrain: 12,384 not_in_village (chars listed in stale world frames after walking home) + 4,626 unknown_character (commands to CORPSES). And the six banked ZERO XP because the embark picker broke on here_avail[0] whatever its role — 3 pair-embarks in 54k frames.
evidence: #177 action_errors by reason; seat field-share 28/121,528 char-frames (0.0%). #178 early: unknown_character 18-pace (-99.6%), pair-embarks 5 in 4.4k frames (~20x), seat field-share 2.4%.
so_what: Frames arrive per-world: a transitioning char is double-listed and a corpse lingers — dead uids never act again, returned chars get a 4-tick grace. Wizard deaths on #177 were ZERO (61 corpses all non-seats): the protection stack is fully proven.

title: The portal network is an express elevator between the spawn strip and the deep map — and it has been acting on us INVOLUNTARILY: 11 accidental transits in runs 170-178 (e.g. (63,1)->(24,126), one row from the village exit to y=126), because nav treats portal tiles as ordinary floor and no decision has ever mentioned one.
evidence: 1,414 portal events all-time; ~20 distinct from->to pairs, overwhelmingly shallow<->deep ((34,5)<->(40,161) bidirectional x45/x43); 17 portal tiles mapped in vale; transit eids joined to our per-run eids = 11 of ours; 0 decisions LIKE '%portal%'.
so_what: Two levers: portal-aware routing (a portal tile is an EDGE to its twin — the graph is learnable from our own events; deep access for the cost of a walk to y=5) and, until then, hazard-masking (a bare char stepping on one is teleported past the poison line — likely the source of old impossible-max-y sightings and shallow chars dying deep). Also: deep MOBS arrive shallow through portals — a fresh hypothesis for sudden band danger.

title: ML Pass 1 shipped: the feature/label substrate — steemer/mlfeat.py as the single source of truth (pure stdlib, versioned schema, boundary-pinned death labels, rotation-invariant mob classes) + a one-pass-per-run extractor with guild-filtered death index and deterministic negative sampling, cached per run under the reaper training cache.
detail: Verified against the real corpus: extractor death counts == attribution exactly (runs 176: 6/6, 177: 69/69); labels agree with postmortem.reconstruct_trace on sampled real deaths; 7 substrate mutants killed. Training deps live in a Linux-only uv group; .reaper-train.toml is the second reaper workload.
