title: PORTAL VANISH SPIRAL: a walkable portal on the spawn strip ate the roster — and the server rendered the lost chars as commandable ghosts
body: Run #179 (live at diagnosis, 51k+ frames): from tick ~2,170,000 scope errors exploded (not_in_village 4,548 — 73% in the last 6% of the run; unknown_character 1,481 across 33 chars; no_such_character embark 900) while real activity collapsed (embarks/2k-ticks 1437 -> 112). Cause chain, each link verified in DB: (1) tiles kind='portal' are NOT in nav.SOLID, so pathing walks onto them; (2) a portal sits at vale (63,0) ON the spawn strip; portal events show repeated involuntary transits (63,0)->(57,44) plus (44,6)/(45,10)->(10,70)/(32,83) — e.g. Recruit-18716's eid portaled at t2171428 and died 99 ticks later; (3) transited chars die deep or VANISH from the server's action roster with NO death event (c18762: recruited t2172669, 4 embark events, zero moves, then unknown_character); (4) the server KEEPS RENDERING lost chars in world frames (c18748 present in spire frames at the same ticks the server answered its moves with unknown_character) — so the bot legitimately commands ghosts forever; (5) the recruit gate correctly replaces real losses (119 recruits, 89 in the last 12k ticks; 18 our-deaths) and the replacements walk the same strip into the same portal. title: XP cost formula VERIFIED from recorded spends: cost = 8v*2^(v//10), halved for gifts — 6/6 exact
body: Operator asked what INT costs; the docs formula had never been checked against data (only soft evidence: zero spend_xp bounces ever). Verified now: for the 6 most recent spend_xp sends with clean frame pairs (runs 180-181), xp_before - xp_after == 8*v*2^(v//10) (//2 when the stat is gifted) EXACTLY — gifted str 1->2 paid 4 (x2), ungifted str 1->2 paid 8, gifted end 2->3 paid 8, gifted vit 2->3 paid 8, ungifted end 1->2 paid 8. INT milestones from the verified formula: 1->4 (tome gate) = 48 XP ungifted / 24 gifted; 1->10 = 360/180; 10->20 = 2,320/1,160.

title: The green gate's census predicate NEVER FIRED — median victim lasted 38 ticks; 0.92.1 latches danger on our own corpses instead
body: Run #181 (0.92.0, mature 27.8k frames at diagnosis): 19 our-deaths, same chaser band (delver x8, lava_ant x5), same shallow strip, only 4/19 fodder. Embark->death gaps: median 38 ticks, 13/19 under 47 — killed AT the door, so the gate was open. Cause: _world_is_dangerous requires >=2 melee predators in ONE character's view (COHESION_PRED_DENSE=2) or undead_frac>=0.08 — but a spread-out chaser band kills SERIALLY; each lone recruit sees one delver, so the census never latched while the world ate a recruit every few hundred ticks. FIX (0.92.1): a death of OUR char (uid present in the sightings ledger) latches its world dangerous for DEATH_GATE_TTL=900 ticks — no density threshold, self-clearing, re-latched by every further victim; rival corpses and village deaths latch nothing. Applies to the shared predicate, so gated WIZARDS inherit the same fix. 5 tests, 5/5 mutants killed (latch removed, TTL boundary, rival latch, village latch, world-not-passed). PROCESS LESSON also recorded: the 0.92.0 gate held greens by a silent `continue` — no decision row, no log — so 'did the gate ever fire' was unanswerable from data; the suppressed path needs an observable next time a gate ships.

title: TWO more gate loopholes closed: cheap spend_xp promotes past level<=1 in minutes, and a bare-handed level-5 is a 'guardian' by title and shipped un-gated

Victim sheets at embark: levels 2-5, stats sum 8-11, hand=None on EVERY one. Two loopholes: (1) green required level<=1, but recruits bank cheap spend_xp (8-16 XP/point at v<=2) within minutes of arriving — level is not youth; (2) role_of calls level>=5 a GUARDIAN and the guardian embark branch ran before the gate — c19219 (level 5, bare hands, stats 11) shipped as a 'guardian' and died to the band. 0.92.2: green = bare hands + not fodder, ANY level, ANY title; the guardian branch requires not-green; wizards keep their stricter gate. Fielding continues into un-latched worlds; fodder and the armed field everywhere. Median embark->death gap under 0.92.1 was 81 ticks (vs 38 on 0.92.0) — the latch bought time but not survival; the classifier was the hole. NOTE the arm-throttle is now the binding constraint on fielding breadth: forge-to-arm (M3a) and gold income raise the armed share and thus un-gate the roster.

title: CORRECTION: roster_cap IS server-enforced (1,597 lifetime refusals on recruit) — but it counts VILLAGE-PRESENT chars, not total roster, which is how we sit at 31
body: Supersedes the earlier 'soft cap / server accepted past cap' finding, which was WRONG: the server refuses recruit with a `roster_cap` action_error and has done so 1,597 times across runs. What it counts is the lever: on #184, recruits SUCCEEDED at apparent totals of 31-33 (village 22-30 + fielded), and there are 0 roster_cap refusals while the true roster is 31. So the server's recruit check is against chars PHYSICALLY IN THE VILLAGE (the barracks), not village+fielded. Consequence: with k chars fielded, total roster can reach ~30+k by recruiting to refill the emptied village. NOT a display bug — the 31 is real (village 30 fresh + c19280 fielded in vale). Whether the village-only count is intended (a barracks cap) or a bug (cap meant as total) is undetermined; logged to server_bugs.md as an observation. NOT EXPLOITED: more characters is the opposite of what the roster needs — 5/30 armed, gold-starved, leveling already diluted; deliberately over-recruiting would worsen the arm-rate constraint the 0.91-0.93 arc exists to relieve. Operator decision if ever wanted.

title: Party-tab '[object Object]' was OUR dashboard bug surfacing on arming, NOT an API change — equipment slots have always been objects
body: Operator reported gear showing [object Object] in the Party tab. Cause: a frame equipment slot is an OBJECT ({item_id, kind, tier, bulk, uses, desc}) — the reference kit's AGENTS.md has documented this shape all along, and the submodule is CURRENT (pin 588702a == origin/HEAD, no upstream commits to pull). The dashboard's pcCard did esc(eq[slot]) directly, which only ever ran on non-null slots — and slots were null until the 0.92.x arming finally equipped chars with clubs, at which point esc(object) printed [object Object]. So a latent bug, revealed by our own progress, not a server change. Fix: reduce each slot to its .kind server-side in api_roster (new _slot_kind helper), mirroring how inventory already does it; tolerant of object / legacy-string / null. The BOT's armed check ((eq or {}).get('hand') truthiness) was always correct — a dict is truthy — so the green gate and equip logic were never affected. 3 tests incl. an end-to-end api_roster oracle (a _slot_kind unit test alone would have stayed green while the panel broke, because the bug was the DROPPED call-site application); mutants 2/2 killed.

title: Ride probe was UNREACHABLE (0 sends on #184) — 0.93.1 routes a qualified prober to the nearest known rail so the experiment can actually run
body: Slice 1 (0.93.0) offered `ride` only from a char ALREADY standing on a track — a coincidence that never happened: #184 logged 0 ride sends, and our armed chars never crossed a track tile (they field shallow while the mines rails sit y12-82; 47 known track tiles, nearest at (2,12)). That is the starvation-by-unreachable-behaviour trap. 0.93.1 adds slice-2 routing: a qualified prober (armed, hp>=70%, sta>=15, calm, not-yet-probed — factored into _ride_prober_ready, shared by seek AND fire so they can't drift) walks toward the nearest known RIDEABLE rail (a track with a track neighbour, so the ride has a direction) at score 3.1 (below harvest 3.3 / gather, above frontier 2.5) within RIDE_SEEK_RANGE=24. Found and fixed a stranding bug in the draft: the first guard (pos != 'track') would freeze a prober parked on a LONE track instead of letting it seek a real rail — replaced with 'not on a rideable rail' via the shared _is_rideable_rail predicate. 5 new tests (12 total in the file); mutants 4/4 killed incl. the observable lone-track stranding case (the on-rail micro-guard was an equivalent mutant — the fire's 4.5 always outranks the seek's 3.1 — so it was retired rather than tested vacuously). Reachability gate caught the new behaviour; registered.

title: The arch-wizard death is a SELF-DEFEATING LOOP: protection slows the int-gifted char's leveling, slow leveling costs it the seat (level outranks the int-gift), losing the seat removes protection, unprotected it dies deep
body: Operator's int-gifted arch-wizard candidate (c19254, gifts str+int, INT 2, lvl 3) died on #184 at vale (4,47) — deep, stuck, hp 4, killed by a crab while doing the hurt move/rest shuffle home ('walking home to heal'). Decisions over its life: 43 WIZARD + 49 FORAGER — its role OSCILLATED, and it died in a forager phase (bold, ranged to y47). Root cause in wizard_rank_key = (-int, -LEVEL, int-gift, -stats, uid): among INT-2 chars, LEVEL is ranked ABOVE the int-gift. A protected wizard is cautious and passive, so it levels SLOWER than bold foragers/fodder who spend XP on combat stats; those chars out-level it and displace it from the top-6 seat; demoted to forager it loses all wizard protection, ranges deep, and dies — throwing away the one char worth investing in (the gift halves every INT point, the ceiling-breaker). The ordering is faithful to the operator's verbatim spec ('chosen by int; tie -> level -> other stats'), but it CONFLICTS with their stated GOAL (max int on chosen chars, break the glass ceiling): the spec's level-first tiebreak evicts exactly the char the goal wants to protect. Whole program still stuck at INT 2 (glass ceiling unbroken). LEVER options for operator: (a) rank int-GIFT above level for seat selection; (b) role hysteresis — a char that has been a seat keeps wizard caution/protection even when momentarily out-ranked; (c) an int-gifted designate never plays bold forager (floor its caution). Reported, not shipped — touches the operator's explicit ordering + chosen-six doctrine.

title: 0.94.0 (operator go): int-GIFT above level in the seat ranking + light hysteresis — breaks the arch-wizard self-defeating loop
body: Operator approved (1)+(light 2) after the #184 arch-wizard death. (1) wizard_rank_key reordered (-int, GIFT, -level, -stats, uid): the int-gift now outranks level, so a protected (slow-leveling) int-gifted char no longer loses its seat to bold higher-level non-gifted chars — the eviction that removed its protection and got it killed. (2) LIGHT HYSTERESIS in select_wizards(chars, cap, incumbents): an incumbent that dips within HYSTERESIS_SLACK=2 ranks of the cutoff reclaims its seat from the newcomer that edged it, via a RANK-GAP rule (pos[inc]-pos[displaced] <= SLACK) — so a clearly-superior newcomer (new high-INT char) is never blocked, only a near-tie is held steady. The strategy holds last tick's seats as the incumbent set (self._wizard_incumbents); empty on a restart's first frame -> pure top-cap, then stabilises (same graceful degrade as the pool floor). Bugs caught in build: my first hysteresis draft (incumbents-fill-first) let stale bench dummies BLOCK a superior newcomer — the picker test caught it; rewrote to the rank-gap rule. Removed a provably-redundant window bound (the gap check already enforces the slack — one source of truth). NOTE: the dashboard still shows pure top-6 (no incumbent memory across processes), so panel and strategy can differ transiently at the churn boundary; self-heals, not worth cross-process sync. 6 wizard-seat tests (3 new hysteresis); mutants 6/6 killed incl. the reclaim + slack-bound cases. Whole roster still INT 2 — glass ceiling unbroken; this protects the ceiling-breaker candidate so it can climb.

title: The idle village: the death latch benches the bare-handed 28/30 for 900 ticks per world on a SINGLE deep death — the gates work, but the latch is world-global where it should be band-local
body: Operator: 'where have all my peeps gone.' Snapshot #186: 30 home, 3 fielded. Timeline shows it CYCLES: 7-8 fielded -> two chars die deep (c19274 at (42,24), c19285 the INT-2 arch-wizard at (56,15)) -> their worlds death-latch for 900 ticks -> the 28/30 BARE-HANDED chars are green-gated home (only ~2 armed + fodder stay out, fielded drops to 3) -> latch expires -> 11 surge back out. Two compounding causes: (1) ARM RATE — 28/30 unarmed (gold-starved below the 150 floor), so almost nobody can enter a dangerous world; (2) the death latch is WORLD-GLOBAL — one death anywhere in vale latches ALL of vale, including the safe shallow spawn strip (y0-10) where a bare forager works fine, for 900 ticks. Net: the protection stack traded 60+ deaths/3-runs for ~2, but the price is a mostly-benched roster generating no income/XP while unarmed. NOT a bug — the gates are doing exactly what they were built to do; it's the arm-rate bottleneck made visible, sharpened by a coarse latch. TWO LEVERS for operator: (A) BAND-LOCAL latch — latch only the y-strip where the death happened, not the whole world, so shallow foragers keep working while the deep band cools (directly un-benches the roster without re-exposing it); (B) ARM the roster — forge-to-arm (M3a) or gold income raises the armed share so chars field into latched worlds. Reported, not shipped — loosening the latch touches the protection stack that just hit zero-death runs.

title: FORGE-TO-ARM is UNBLOCKED: spear recipe PROVEN (1 lumber + 1 ingot_copper), we forged one on #186 — 0.95.0 forges a WEAPON first for a bare hand
body: Chasing the idle-village + passive-char reports (both root-caused to 28/30 bare-handed) to the forge chain: it's further along than the HANDOFF said. On #186 our char c19282 forged a SPEAR — forge {product:'spear', item_ids:[442133 =lumber, 442508=ingot_copper]} — so the 'undiscovered product name' that deferred M3a is moot (forge_started carries `product`; spear/dagger/shortsword are weapons, shield_iron is armour). The recipe is now KNOWN and materials are ones we already make (chop tree->lumber, smelt 2 ore->ingot). Chain verified end to end: chop/smelt -> forge (proven recipe, _forge_proven) -> equip fills empty slots. The GAP was PRIORITY: FORGE_PRODUCTS led with shield_iron (armour, correct when 100% offhands were empty and armour was the crisis), so scarce materials became shields while hands stayed empty. 0.95.0: a char with an EMPTY HAND forges FORGE_WEAPON_FIRST (spear, shortsword, dagger, then shield) — same tuple contents so every recipe/proven/failed key still applies, only the order flips; an armed char still forges the unbuyable shield. Directly attacks the arm rate underlying BOTH operator reports. 2 forge tests updated + 1 new (dynamic priority); 3/3 mutants killed; two sibling tests de-vacuum'd (they'd have passed for an unrelated reason under the new order). NOTE 535 wrong_materials are the blind recipe-ladder search; with the spear recipe proven that thrash drops. NEXT: measure #187 armed-share climb + fewer bare-handed benched.

title: THE NUISANCE (0.96.0, operator): a yellow role that shadows rival WillMorr's party in the vale, helps kill, loots his fallen, and cackles the spoils home
body: Operator-directed fun feature, built live across six messages. WillMorr = guild g_63837f (his chars are named Barbarian/Ranger/Harvester/Miner — that's why searching 'WillMorr' in char names found nothing). He is NOT currently fielded (0 rival chars visible; the track feed showing him is stale), so this is a 'when Will shows up' feature — built reachable, verified entirely by unit tests (Will absent = can't live-test). Spec: (1) a new display role 'nuisance', YELLOW (#e3b341); (2) trigger when >=3 of Will's chars share the vale -> one of our chars volunteers; (3) SHADOW phase: greedy-step to hang within 2 of his party centroid (the centroid tile is usually one of his chars, blocked); helps kill via positioning + the existing develop-fight; (4) says ':(' when a Will char attacks it (attacker eid in the learned Will-eid set); (5) reclassify when Will leaves the vale (GONE_TTL=40) or the nuisance dies (relief takes over at once); re-designate on his return; (6) LOOT phase: a Will member dies with a drop -> beeline to it; (7) on a real pickup EVENT (only if successful) -> DELIVER: cackle 'mwahahahaha' (score 6.1, wins the first tick) then beeline home; reaching the village banks the spoils (the sell economy even funds the arm rate) and completes the tour. Survival outranks every nuisance offer (3.6-6.1 < flee/heal 8.0+), so 'try not to die' holds by construction. The nuisance uid is recorded to intel(kind='nuisance') so the dashboard (which can't see runtime state) can paint it yellow. 15 tests, all phases + reclassifications; 8/8 mutants killed. BUGS caught in build: rival guild chars are ctx.bodies blockers (the centroid is on one) -> greedy step + proximity goal; my test _DIR was inverted (this game N=+y) -> the behaviour was right all along; optimistic loot->deliver flip violated 'only if successful' -> made it pickup-event-driven.

title: HINTS: the bot now consumes the sidecar's map-wide rival positions — the nuisance couldn't see Will because it used only LOCAL vision + the sidecar's track feed had a dead DB connection
body: Operator: 'Will is in the vale and I don't see a nuisance.' Two root causes. (1) The track recorder (rival positions via SSE) was crash-looping on 'MySQL Connection not available' — its DB connection died (stale after the LAN exposure) while the sidecar's OTHER writers (spectate, color) kept flowing on the healthy main connection, so the watchdog's any-intel heartbeat never noticed. A sidecar restart revived it (track tick 1673777 -> live). (2) Deeper: the nuisance read only frame.visible.entities (LOCAL vision), and our 5 vale chars were shallow-NE while Will's 5 were deep-SW — never in sight. Fix (operator's idea): the bot accepts HINTS from the feed-watcher. GuildBot._refresh_hints() reads the latest track intel every HINT_REFRESH_TICKS=8 into bot.rival_hints {world: [{guild_id,pos,name}]} (cached, fail-closed). The nuisance now DETECTS Will map-wide (>=3 of his chars in the vale by hint OR local vision) and ROUTES toward his hint centroid when he's unseen locally, switching to exact local positions once in sight. This is a general capability (rival recon, threat avoidance can all use hints), not just the nuisance. 8 new tests (4 hint-reader, 4 nuisance-hint), all mutation-checked; a directional test trap (a deep char heads home regardless) was fixed by asserting the WINNING action's reasoning, not just its direction. STILL OWED (operator asked): a TRACK-SPECIFIC sidecar heartbeat so the watchdog restarts it when the track feed alone goes stale (the any-intel heartbeat masks it).

title: THE ARM-RATE BOTTLENECK is material+location CONVERGENCE, not forge priority: 0/28 bare chars are forge-ready and the forge is deep in the mines
body: Traced the arm rate to its root on #189. shield_iron dominated our forge queue (418 attempts vs 7 spear, ~421 wrong_materials) for a specific reason: only 1 of 30 chars forges (c19350), and it holds a PICKAXE — the 0.95.0 weapon-first check reads hand_empty=False (a tool fills the hand), routes it to the ARMOR-first path, and it forges shield_iron every cycle, failing wrong_materials (it feeds a copper/iron ingot mix the recipe rejects). Defect 1: a TOOL counts as a weapon. The 28 bare-handed chars weapon-first was built for CANNOT forge: 0/28 are forge-ready (a spear needs 1 lumber AND 1 ingot on ONE char; only 1 bare char has an ingot, 2 have lumber, NONE have both), and the only known forge tiles are DEEP in the mines (y105-117) while 20/30 chars sit in the village. Defect 2 (the real one): CONVERGENCE — lumber (chopped on the surface/vale) and ingots (smelted from mines ore) never combine on one character at the deep forge. CATCH-22: the forge is deep in danger, but our own survival gates (death-latch, green-gate) correctly keep bare chars OUT of deep danger — so the chars that need weapons can't safely reach the place that makes them. The 0.95.0 weapon-first change was cosmetic: it reordered a queue only one wrong-handed char ever reaches. FIX (smith pipeline): (A) a tool-hand still forges a weapon; (B) a forge-ready char seeks the nearest forge; (C, slice 2) material staging so lumber+ingot converge on a smith.

title: SMITH PIPELINE slice 1 shipped: tool-hand forges a weapon + ingot-holders withdraw stash lumber to converge materials
body: Fixes the #189 arm-rate bottleneck (0/28 forge-ready; a lone pickaxe-miner spamming failed shields). (A) FORGE_HAND_TOOLS: a pickaxe/sickle in hand no longer reads as armed, so the forger makes a spear not a shield_iron. (B) material convergence: a village char with an ingot but no lumber withdraws a lumber from the guild stash (19 sat unused; ingots are the scarce half), vault-dead-guarded. Corrected the earlier 'deep-mines forge' claim — all forging is village-based (village forge exists; mines tiles were a red herring), so location was never the blocker, materials were. 6 tests, 6/6 mutants killed. SLICE 2 deferred: ingot SCARCITY (only smelted from mines ore) is the remaining convergence limit. Measure #190: armed share off 2/30?

title: Smith pipeline slice 1 MEASURED: the forge THRASH is gone (418->0 shield, 421->0 wrong_materials) but arming is still 2/30 — INGOT SCARCITY is a FIELDING problem, nobody mines ore
body: #190 (0.98.0, mature 33k frames): Fix A worked cleanly — forge attempts collapsed from 418 shield_iron/7 spear to 2 spear/0 shield, and wrong_materials 421->0. The waste is eliminated. But armed share is STILL 2/30 because the forge barely fires: only 4 smelt attempts, 2 chars hold an ingot, 1 holds ore, 0 forge-ready, and Fix B (lumber withdrawal) fired 0 times (its ingot-holders were few and the stash had 20 lumber but 0 ingots). ROOT: ingot production is ~nil because nobody mines ore. Role x world: 24/30 benched in the VILLAGE (14 forager, 4 wizard, 6 guardian), only 6 fielded, and just 1 char in the mines where the 65 vein tiles (ore) are. The fielding dispatcher routes gatherers to the SAFEST/least-crowded world — the surface vale (trees=lumber), NOT the mines (veins=ore) — so the lumber/ingot asymmetry is really a fielding asymmetry. And the survival gates (death-latch, green-gate) bench the bare majority, so the vicious cycle closes: bare -> benched -> don't mine -> no ore -> no ingots -> no weapons -> stay bare. LEVER (0.99.0): ORE-HUNGRY FIELDING — when ingot-poor, bias forager/fodder embark toward the ore world (mines), within the green-gate (bare only into a calm mines; fodder exempt as the designed risk-taker). Ore is the bootstrap resource; without it the smith pipeline has nothing to forge.

title: ORE-HUNGRY FIELDING shipped: ingot-poor guild routes gatherers to the ore world
body: Slice 2 of the arm-rate fix. #190 proved the smith pipeline's thrash-fix (A) worked but ingots are absent because nobody mines (1 char in the mines; the dispatcher sends gatherers to the safe surface for lumber, not the mines for ore). Now: INGOT_HUNGRY (<=3 stash ingots) biases a forager/fodder embark to the ore world, derived from seen vein tiles, inside the green-gate. Self-correcting. 4 tests, 4/4 mutants. Measure #191: mines headcount + smelts + armed share.

title: Ore-dispatch mine-worthy gate: only fodder/armed mine the mines; bare foragers and wizards stay safe
body: #191: 'only one char deployed' = a revolving door (205 embarks / 15 chars, one 58x, median 38-tick stints, 15 never field). v0.99.0's ore bias worsened it by sending BARE foragers to the mines to churn. 0.99.1: ore dispatch only routes MINE-WORTHY chars (fodder or armed) to the mines; bare foragers stay on the surface. Wizards are double-protected — their own escort/band gate runs first, so the ore work never touches them (explicit test). 8 ore tests, mine-worthy mutants 3/3. The revolving door is the arm-rate problem; this stops the dispatch feeding it.

title: The arm rate was a STALE GOLD FLOOR: WEAPON_BUY_FLOOR=150 while gold sat at ~85 — the guild bought NO weapons for runs while clubs sat in the shop
body: The whole forge saga (0.95-0.99.1) was working around a frozen reserve. #192: WEAPON_BUY_FLOOR=150 (comment: 'we sit at ~600'), but the guild is chronically at ~85 gold — BELOW all three floors (POTION 100 / WEAPON 150 / ARMOR 200) — so it bought nothing. The shop STOCKS 15g clubs. Fix: recalibrate to the coin-dry reality (POTION_RESERVE 30 / WEAPON 45 / ARMOR 70, ordering kept), so a bare char arms with a shop club at 85 gold (heals first, then arms). BONUS: the tome-buy line = tome_price + POTION_RESERVE drops 220 -> 150, magic reachable sooner. 7 tests (6 floor-pins updated + 1 new coin-dry arming); weapon-floor mutant killed. The forge chain still matters for tier-2 gear the shop lacks, but the BOOTSTRAP was always: lower the floor and buy a club.
